nodes.description: E3 ubiquitin ligase and principal negative regulator of p53. AKT phosphorylates MDM2 at Ser166/Ser186, promoting its nuclear entry and p53 turnover; this is the survival arm of AKT output biased by mTORC2-dependent Ser473 phosphorylation.

nodes.label: ChREBP
nodes.description: Carbohydrate-response element-binding protein; adipose mTORC2 drives ChREBP-dependent de novo lipogenesis, with consequences for hepatic glucose metabolism.

nodes.label: NDRG1
nodes.description: N-myc downstream-regulated gene 1 product; SGK1 substrate at Thr346/356/366 and the standard cellular readout of mTORC2–SGK1 activity.

nodes.label: Nedd4-2
nodes.description: HECT-domain E3 ubiquitin ligase that ubiquitinates ENaC subunits and promotes their retrieval from the apical membrane; inactivated by SGK1 phosphorylation and 14-3-3 binding.

nodes.label: Rac1
nodes.description: Rho-family GTPase driving branched actin polymerisation, lamellipodia and dendritic spine remodelling; activated downstream of mTORC2 via Tiam1 and downstream of PKC signalling.

nodes.label: RhoA
nodes.description: Rho-family GTPase controlling stress fibres, actomyosin contractility and adhesion; part of the Rho-family signalling affected when mTORC2-dependent PKC protein is lost.

nodes.label: ENaC
nodes.description: Epithelial sodium channel of the aldosterone-sensitive distal nephron; principal effector through which mTORC2–SGK1 sets sodium reabsorption and blood pressure.

nodes.label: GLUT4
nodes.description: Insulin-responsive glucose transporter of muscle and adipose tissue; its translocation to the plasma membrane is the proximate step in insulin-stimulated glucose uptake.

nodes.label: AS160 (TBC1D4)
nodes.description: Rab GAP that restrains GLUT4 vesicle translocation; AKT phosphorylation at Thr642 creates a 14-3-3 site and relieves this restraint, permitting insulin-stimulated glucose uptake.

nodes.label: Tiam1
nodes.description: Rac1-specific guanine nucleotide exchange factor; the mTORC2 effector through which forebrain mTORC2 drives actin polymerisation required for consolidation of long-term memory.

nodes.label: BMAL1 (ARNTL)
nodes.description: Core clock bHLH-PAS transcription factor; heterodimerises with CLOCK to drive E-box transcription. Also a negative regulator of mTORC1 and, when phosphorylated by S6K1, a promoter of rhythmic cap-dependent translation.

nodes.label: CLOCK
nodes.description: Core clock bHLH-PAS transcription factor and obligate BMAL1 partner; the CLOCK–BMAL1 heterodimer drives E-box-dependent transcription of Per, Cry and many metabolic output genes.

nodes.label: CLOCK–BMAL1 heterodimer
nodes.description: Positive limb transcription factor of the mammalian clock; binds E-boxes to activate Per1/Per2, Cry1/Cry2 and clock-controlled output genes, and is repressed by the PER–CRY complex it induces.

nodes.label: CRY1 (Cryptochrome 1)
nodes.description: Negative-limb clock protein; partners PER to repress CLOCK–BMAL1. Its stability is set by AMPK-dependent phosphorylation and FBXL3-mediated degradation, making it an energy-sensitive clock node.

nodes.label: Casein kinase 1ε (CSNK1E)
nodes.description: PER-directed kinase controlling PER2 stability and nuclear entry; the node through which AMPK (an mTOR-pathway energy sensor) reaches the clock.

nodes.label: REV-ERBα (NR1D1)
nodes.description: Nuclear receptor of the accessory clock loop; CLOCK–BMAL1 target that represses Bmal1 transcription through RORE elements, generating the antiphase BMAL1 rhythm.

nodes.label: PER1 (Period 1)
nodes.description: Negative-limb clock protein and immediate-early photic response gene in the SCN; its light-induced expression is attenuated by mTOR inhibition, linking mTOR to phase shifting.

nodes.label: PER–CRY repressor complex
nodes.description: Heteromeric PER–CRY complex of the negative limb; formed in the cytoplasm, enters the nucleus and represses CLOCK–BMAL1.

nodes.label: VIP (vasoactive intestinal peptide)
nodes.description: Neuropeptide of SCN core neurons required for synchrony and rhythmicity of the SCN network; its translation in the SCN is under 4E-BP1 control and therefore sensitive to mTORC1 activity.

nodes.label: Amyloid-beta
nodes.description: Aggregation-prone peptide whose brain burden falls with autophagy induction; rapamycin lowers it in 3xTg-AD mice when given before substantial pathology.

nodes.label: Huntingtin (polyQ)
nodes.description: Polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin, an autophagy substrate reduced by rapamycin or CCI-779 in fly and mouse models.

nodes.label: alpha-Synuclein
nodes.description: Aggregation-prone synaptic protein cleared by macroautophagy.

nodes.label: Cap-dependent translation
nodes.description: eIF4F-dependent initiation on 5'-capped mRNAs, preferentially affecting transcripts with structured 5' UTRs; only partially suppressed by rapalogs because Thr37/Thr46 of 4E-BP1 resist them.

nodes.label: Cell growth (mass/size)
nodes.description: Increase in cell mass and size driven by the S6K-rpS6 axis and ribosome biogenesis; distinct from proliferation, which depends on the 4E-BP arm.

nodes.label: Cell proliferation
nodes.description: mTORC1-dependent proliferation controlled by the 4E-BP-eIF4E arm (cyclin D1, c-Myc translation) rather than by S6K-dependent cell growth.

nodes.label: Protein synthesis
nodes.description: mTORC1-dependent anabolic response of skeletal muscle to loading and to essential amino acids; blocked in humans by acute rapamycin, and the basis of the anabolic-resistance concern in older adults.

nodes.label: Ribosome biogenesis
nodes.description: Coordinated production of rRNA (Pol I), 5S rRNA and tRNA (Pol III) and ribosomal proteins (Pol II/TOP translation) scaled by mTORC1 and S6K1.

nodes.label: adipogenesis
nodes.description: Differentiation and lipid-storage programme of adipocytes requiring mTORC1; adipocyte Raptor deletion impairs adipogenesis and reduces fat mass.

nodes.label: Autophagic lysosome reformation
nodes.description: Tubulation and scission of autolysosomes that regenerates functional lysosomes at the end of an autophagic cycle; it requires mTOR reactivation driven by degradation-derived amino acids [686]. This reactivation is the mechanistic basis of the oscillatory behaviour of mTORC1 activity during prolonged autophagy.

nodes.label: autophagy
nodes.description: Macroautophagic sequestration and lysosomal degradation of cytoplasmic material; one of the two principal catabolic arms repressed by mTORC1, and the arm with greatest consequence in post-mitotic tissue.

nodes.label: cholesterol synthesis
nodes.description: SREBP2-driven sterol biosynthetic programme requiring mTOR activity; partially rapamycin-resistant at the transcriptional level.

nodes.label: CLEAR gene network
nodes.description: Coordinated Lysosomal Expression And Regulation network of approximately 470 lysosomal and autophagy genes driven by TFEB/TFE3 through a palindromic E-box promoter motif.

nodes.label: glutamine anaplerosis
nodes.description: Replenishment of TCA-cycle intermediates from glutamine-derived alpha-ketoglutarate, supported downstream of mTORC1 by the S6K1-GDH axis and by c-Myc.

nodes.label: glutathione synthesis
nodes.description: ATF4-dependent production of glutathione downstream of mTORC1, linking growth signalling to redox buffering alongside protein synthesis.

nodes.label: glycolysis
nodes.description: Glycolytic flux; supported by hepatic mTORC2 via AKT and glucokinase, and required (with glutaminolysis) for effector T-cell metabolic reprogramming.

nodes.label: de novo lipogenesis
nodes.description: SREBP1-driven fatty-acid synthesis downstream of mTORC1; in liver it is the basis of mTORC1-associated steatosis and of rapalog-associated dyslipidaemia.

nodes.label: lysosomal biogenesis
nodes.description: TFEB/TFE3-driven expansion of lysosomal number and degradative capacity through the CLEAR network; suppressed by mTORC1.

nodes.label: mitochondrial biogenesis
nodes.description: Expansion of mitochondrial mass and oxidative capacity supported by 4E-BP-dependent translation of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs and by the YY1-PGC-1alpha transcriptional complex.

nodes.label: one-carbon/folate metabolism
nodes.description: Mitochondrial tetrahydrofolate cycle supplying formyl and methyl units for nucleotide synthesis and methylation reactions; coupled to mTORC1 through ATF4-MTHFD2.

nodes.label: pentose phosphate pathway
nodes.description: Oxidative branch activated through SREBP-driven G6PD expression; supplies NADPH for reductive biosynthesis and ribose-5-phosphate for nucleotides.

nodes.label: de novo purine synthesis
nodes.description: Purine nucleotide production driven by mTORC1 through ATF4-dependent control of the mitochondrial tetrahydrofolate cycle.

nodes.label: de novo pyrimidine synthesis
nodes.description: Pyrimidine nucleotide production stimulated acutely by the S6K1-CAD Ser1859 axis downstream of mTORC1.

nodes.label: senescence-associated secretory phenotype
nodes.description: Pro-inflammatory secretome of senescent cells, which requires mTORC1-driven translation (IL1A; MAPKAPK2); rapamycin suppresses the SASP without eliminating senescent cells, an example of geroprotective benefit without causal primacy.

nodes.label: Actin cytoskeleton
nodes.description: Actin filament organisation and polymerisation; the founding mTORC2-dependent output, driven through Rho-family GTPases, PKC isoforms and Tiam1–Rac1.

nodes.label: Cell adhesion
nodes.description: Cell–matrix and cell–cell adhesion dynamics downstream of PKC and Rho-family signalling, reduced in mTORC2-deficient cells.

nodes.label: Cell migration
nodes.description: Directed cell motility dependent on cytoskeletal remodelling; impaired when mTORC2-dependent PKC protein and Rho-family signalling are lost.

nodes.label: Cell survival signalling
nodes.description: Anti-apoptotic programme sustained by AKT phosphorylation of BAD and of FOXO transcription factors; the arm of AKT output most dependent on mTORC2-mediated Ser473 phosphorylation.

nodes.label: Epithelial polarity
nodes.description: Apicobasal organisation of epithelial sheets, established largely through atypical PKC in the Par3–Par6 module and therefore dependent on mTORC2-mediated PKC maturation.

nodes.label: Insulin-stimulated glucose uptake
nodes.description: GLUT4-mediated glucose entry into muscle and adipose tissue following insulin; reduced by adipose Rictor deletion and by chronic mTORC2 loss.

nodes.label: Distal nephron ion transport
nodes.description: Transepithelial sodium, potassium and chloride handling in the distal nephron, set by SGK1-dependent regulation of ENaC, the Na+/K+-ATPase and CLC-K channels.

nodes.label: Lipolysis
nodes.description: Hydrolysis of stored triacylglycerol in adipocytes. An adipose mTORC2-dependent output alongside insulin-stimulated glucose uptake; adipocyte Rictor deletion alters lipid handling.

nodes.label: Late-phase LTP (L-LTP)
nodes.description: Protein-synthesis-dependent late phase of hippocampal long-term potentiation and the long-term memory that depends on it; rapamycin-sensitive, whereas early-phase LTP and short-term memory are spared.

nodes.label: CNS myelination
nodes.description: Formation and maintenance of oligodendrocyte myelin sheaths in the central nervous system. Oligodendrocyte-lineage deletion separates the complexes: Raptor loss causes persistent hypomyelination, Rictor loss has modest and largely transient effects, and only the double mutant impairs oligodendrocyte differentiation.

nodes.label: Th2 effector differentiation
nodes.description: Differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells into Th2 effector cells. Selectively dependent on Rictor-mTORC2, in contrast to Th1/Th17 differentiation, which depends on Rheb-mTORC1.

nodes.label: Foxp3+ regulatory T cell differentiation
nodes.description: Differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells into Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. Restrained by both mTOR complexes; loss of mTOR kinase activity promotes it, which is the basis of preferential Treg expansion under rapamycin.

nodes.label: Circadian clock (transcription–translation feedback loop)
nodes.description: Cell-autonomous ~24 h oscillator built from the CLOCK–BMAL1 activator limb and the PER/CRY repressor limb; entrained centrally by light and peripherally by feeding, and reciprocally coupled to mTORC1.

nodes.label: Glutaminolysis
nodes.description: Glutamine catabolism supporting anaplerosis; part of the metabolic reprogramming of effector T-cell activation that requires both mTOR complexes.

nodes.label: Insulin secretion
nodes.description: Glucose-stimulated insulin release from pancreatic beta-cells. Insulin secretion and beta-cell survival are the mTORC2-dependent outputs of the beta-cell; reduced secretion is part of the mechanism of rapamycin-associated NODAT.

nodes.label: Ketogenesis
nodes.description: Hepatic production of ketone bodies during fasting; a liver mTORC1-dependent output. mTORC1 suppresses fasting ketogenesis via PPARalpha/NCoR1.

nodes.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome
nodes.description: Autosomal dominant syndrome of fibrofolliculomas, pulmonary cysts with pneumothorax and renal tumours caused by FLCN loss.

nodes.label: GATOR1-related focal epilepsy (FFEVF)
nodes.description: Familial focal epilepsies caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in DEPDC5, NPRL2 or NPRL3, with elevated SUDEP risk; everolimus titrated to troughs of 5-15 ng/mL gave genotype-dependent, mixed results in small open-label series. Graded emerging, in explicit contrast to established everolimus in TSC.

nodes.label: SZT2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
nodes.description: Infantile encephalopathy with epilepsy, intellectual disability, macrocephaly and a dysmorphic corpus callosum, caused by biallelic SZT2 mutations.

nodes.label: Age-associated memory impairment
nodes.description: Decline in long-term memory with age; reversed in mice and flies by a small molecule that raises mTORC2 activity, which also enhances L-LTP in wild-type animals.

nodes.label: Whole-body growth
nodes.description: Organismal body size and growth trajectory. Adipose-tissue mTORC2 negatively controls whole-body growth, so adipocyte Rictor deletion increases body size - a direction of effect opposite to the usual anabolic framing of mTOR signalling.

nodes.label: Glucose intolerance / insulin resistance
nodes.description: Impaired systemic glucose handling arising chiefly from mTORC2 loss: liver-specific Rictor deletion produces a type-2-diabetes-like phenotype, and chronic rapamycin reproduces it pharmacologically.

nodes.label: Hypotension
nodes.description: Low systemic arterial pressure resulting from impaired distal nephron sodium reabsorption. Reported together with salt wasting on renal mTORC2 loss, downstream of failed SGK1-dependent activation of ENaC, Na+/K+-ATPase and CLC-K.

nodes.label: Long-term memory consolidation
nodes.description: Persistent memory formation requiring late-phase LTP; selectively impaired by forebrain Rictor deletion while short-term memory is spared.

nodes.label: Salt wasting and hypotension
nodes.description: Distal-nephron phenotype of renal mTORC2 loss, mediated by failure of SGK1-dependent ENaC and Na+/K+-ATPase regulation; the predicted electrolyte disturbance of mTORC2 inhibition in kidney.

nodes.label: Pancreatic β-cell
nodes.description: Islet cell type in which both complexes are required; β-cell Rictor deletion causes mild hyperglycaemia with reduced β-cell mass, lower AKT Ser473 phosphorylation and nuclear FOXO1 accumulation.

nodes.label: CNS neuron
nodes.description: Forebrain neurons in which mTORC2 supports actin-dependent consolidation of long-term memory and spine density; the only tissue where mTORC2 loss produces a cognitive rather than metabolic deficit.

nodes.label: Cardiomyocyte
nodes.description: Cardiac muscle cell in which mTORC2 is cytoprotective during ischaemia–reperfusion through AKT-dependent anti-apoptotic signalling, so that dual inhibitors are predicted to be more cardiotoxic.

nodes.label: Renal tubule (distal nephron)
nodes.description: Aldosterone-sensitive distal nephron, where mTORC2–SGK1 signalling governs sodium handling; tubular mTORC2 loss produces salt wasting and hypotension.

nodes.label: Skeletal muscle
nodes.description: Tissue in which mTORC1 is dominant and mTORC2 largely dispensable: muscle-specific Rictor deletion is close to phenotypically silent while Raptor deletion causes dystrophy.

nodes.label: Smith–Kingsmore syndrome
nodes.description: Germline gain-of-function MTOR mTORopathy with macrocephaly, intellectual disability and seizures; its phenotype has been extended to include sleep–wake and circadian disturbance, hyperphagia and hyperactivity.

nodes.label: Cellular circadian amplitude
nodes.description: Amplitude of the cellular circadian oscillation, dampened by pathogenic MTOR variants in Smith-Kingsmore syndrome and improved by low-dose rapamycin in engineered U2OS cells expressing SKS-associated MTOR variants.

nodes.label: Circadian behavioural abnormality
nodes.description: Disrupted period, phase or consolidation of locomotor rhythms in rodent models of mTOR hyperactivation; rescued by reducing Bmal1 gene dosage, implicating BMAL1 proteostasis as the mediating lesion.

nodes.label: Circadian period length
nodes.description: Free-running period of molecular and behavioural rhythms; lengthened by mTOR inhibition in SCN explants, fibroblasts and mice [484].

nodes.label: Delayed sleep–wake phase disorder
nodes.description: Circadian rhythm sleep disorder in which habitual sleep onset and offset are shifted substantially later than conventional times; precipitated in some Smith–Kingsmore patients by high-dose rapamycin.

nodes.label: Hyperactivity
nodes.description: Recognised feature of Smith–Kingsmore syndrome in the same cohort [361], reported alongside sleep–wake disturbance.

nodes.label: Hyperphagia
nodes.description: Recognised feature of Smith–Kingsmore syndrome in the 28-individual cohort [361]; mechanistically expected from hypothalamic mTORC1 nutrient sensing.

nodes.label: Photic entrainment
nodes.description: Light-induced phase shifting and re-entrainment of behavioural rhythms; an mTOR-modulated output [79,484].

nodes.label: Premature ageing phenotype
nodes.description: Accelerated age-related pathology (cataracts, organ atrophy, shortened lifespan) seen in Bmal1-null mice and attributed in part to unrestrained mTORC1 signalling.

nodes.label: Sleep–wake disturbance
nodes.description: Disturbed sleep timing, maintenance and quality; a recognised feature of Smith–Kingsmore syndrome and a proposed monitoring endpoint for mTOR-directed therapy.

nodes.label: Suprachiasmatic nucleus
nodes.description: Hypothalamic master pacemaker; receives retinal photic input, synchronises peripheral clocks, and depends on VIP signalling for network synchrony. mTOR signalling here modulates photic entrainment and central clock function.

nodes.label: Alzheimer's disease
nodes.description: Target of the autophagy-based mTOR-inhibition rationale; supported by 3xTg-AD mouse data but with no controlled human efficacy data - the ERAP phase IIa study of weekly oral rapamycin uses FDG-PET cerebral glucose metabolism as its primary outcome.

nodes.label: Renal angiomyolipoma
nodes.description: TSC-associated (or sporadic LAM-associated) renal tumour; EXIST-2 indication, with 42% of everolimus-treated patients achieving at least 50% reduction.

nodes.label: HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer
nodes.description: Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer progressing on an aromatase inhibitor; the single disease in which the mTOR, PI3K and AKT nodes have been tested in separate randomised trials.

nodes.label: Cancer (advanced solid tumours)
nodes.description: Mixed population of advanced solid tumours, 58% carrying pathogenic mTOR-pathway variants, enrolled in the first-in-human bi-steric inhibitor study.

nodes.label: Endometrial carcinoma
nodes.description: Carcinoma with PIK3CA mutation in roughly 30% and PTEN loss in roughly 35% of cases; site of the complete response to RMC-5552.

nodes.label: Focal cortical dysplasia type II
nodes.description: Cortical malformation from somatic mosaic activating variants confined to the dysplastic cortex, with drug-resistant focal epilepsy treated surgically.

nodes.label: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
nodes.description: Glomerular scarring produced in mice by podocyte Tsc1 deletion, the upper limb of the podocyte Goldilocks requirement.

nodes.label: Glioblastoma
nodes.description: PTEN is lost in approximately 40% of glioblastomas, the highest frequency of PTEN loss among these tumour types.

nodes.label: Huntington's disease
nodes.description: Polyglutamine expansion disorder; mTOR inhibition by rapamycin or the ester analogue CCI-779 (temsirolimus) induces autophagy and reduces polyglutamine toxicity in fly and mouse models.

nodes.label: Hemimegalencephaly
nodes.description: Hemispheric brain enlargement with severe epilepsy from somatic mosaic activation of MTOR, PIK3CA or AKT3; mTOR inhibition investigational.

nodes.label: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis
nodes.description: Progressive cystic lung disease driven by TSC2-deficient smooth-muscle-like cells, sporadic or TSC-associated; an approved sirolimus indication.

nodes.label: Neuroendocrine tumour
nodes.description: Well-differentiated pancreatic, gastrointestinal and lung neuroendocrine tumours; a lineage dependency without a defined pathway lesion, treated with everolimus on RADIANT-3 and RADIANT-4.

nodes.label: Parkinson's disease
nodes.description: Alpha-synuclein proteinopathy; rapamycin protects against neuron death in in vitro and in vivo models, with autophagic clearance as the proposed mechanism. Preclinical only.

nodes.label: Malignant PEComa
nodes.description: Malignant PEComa; the nab-sirolimus indication from AMPECT, with response enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours.

nodes.label: PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome
nodes.description: Germline PTEN loss spanning Cowden and Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndromes, with hamartomas, macrocephaly and elevated breast, thyroid and endometrial cancer risk.

nodes.label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
nodes.description: Germline STK11 (LKB1) loss causing hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyposis, mucocutaneous pigmentation and elevated cancer risk.

nodes.label: Polycystic kidney disease
nodes.description: Cystic kidney disease in which elevated mTORC1 activity contributes to cyst growth; trials limited by dose-related toxicity rather than absent rationale.

nodes.label: PMSE syndrome
nodes.description: Polyhydramnios, megalencephaly and symptomatic epilepsy syndrome; autosomal recessive STRADA loss with impaired LKB1-AMPK signalling and mTORC1 hyperactivation; rapamycin reduces seizures (preclinical and small clinical evidence).

nodes.label: PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum
nodes.description: Mosaic somatic PIK3CA activating variants causing segmental overgrowth (CLOVES, megalencephaly-capillary malformation, isolated macrodactyly)

nodes.label: Prostate carcinoma
nodes.description: PTEN is lost in approximately 30% of prostate cancers.

nodes.label: Proteus syndrome
nodes.description: Mosaic overgrowth disorder caused by the somatic activating AKT1 E17K variant

nodes.label: Renal cell carcinoma
nodes.description: Clear-cell renal carcinoma; an approved rapalog indication in which benefit plausibly runs through HIF-dependent translation and the angiogenic programme rather than a cell-autonomous mTORC1 dependency.

nodes.label: Subependymal giant cell astrocytoma
nodes.description: TSC-associated low-grade glioneuronal tumour; the EXIST-1 indication, with roughly 35% of everolimus-treated patients achieving at least 50% volume reduction versus 0% on placebo.

nodes.label: Tuberous sclerosis complex
nodes.description: Germline TSC1 or TSC2 loss with somatic second hits producing SEGA, angiomyolipoma, LAM and epilepsy; the indication in which the rapalog mechanistic rationale is fully borne out.

nodes.label: Urothelial carcinoma
nodes.description: Bladder cancer providing the exceptional-responder evidence for proximal-brake dependency, with TSC1 mutations in roughly 8% of a 109-tumour series.

nodes.label: Anabolic resistance
nodes.description: Blunted muscle protein synthesis response to amino acids and loading in ageing muscle, with elevated basal signalling and attenuated acute response: a compressed dynamic range.

nodes.label: Astrocyte proliferation
nodes.description: Reactive astrocytosis accompanying microglial Tsc1 deletion, alongside reduced synapse density and early-onset spontaneous recurrent seizures.

nodes.label: Autism-like behaviour
nodes.description: Social-interaction and repetitive-behaviour deficits produced by 4E-BP2 loss, demonstrating that excessive as well as deficient translational signalling is deleterious in neurons.

nodes.label: Beta-cell dedifferentiation and failure
nodes.description: Initial expansion of mass and secretion under chronic mTORC1 hyperactivation followed by dedifferentiation through ER stress and suppressed autophagy.

nodes.label: Beta-cell mass and maturation
nodes.description: Functional beta-cell number and maturity; impaired by beta-cell Raptor deletion and reduced, with elevated p27, by beta-cell Rictor deletion.

nodes.label: Physiological cardiac hypertrophy
nodes.description: Adaptive cardiomyocyte growth supported by mTORC1; sustained activity instead contributes to maladaptive remodelling.

nodes.label: Cardiomyocyte cytoprotection
nodes.description: AKT-dependent anti-apoptotic protection of cardiomyocytes during ischaemia-reperfusion, supplied by mTORC2.

nodes.label: CD8 memory T cell quantity and quality
nodes.description: Number and functional quality of memory CD8 T cells generated after acute viral infection; enhanced rather than suppressed by low-dose rapamycin, T cell-intrinsically and across species.

nodes.label: Cellular senescence
nodes.description: Stable cell-cycle arrest with an inflammatory secretome; rapamycin attenuates the consequences of senescence without eliminating senescent cells, so efficacy of an intervention does not establish causal primacy.

nodes.label: Cytopenia
nodes.description: Anaemia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia on rapalogs, attributed to the proliferative requirement for mTORC1 in haematopoiesis.

nodes.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
nodes.description: Fatal phenotype of complete cardiomyocyte mTOR deletion, marking the lower bound of the cardiac therapeutic window.

nodes.label: Fat mass
nodes.description: Whole-body adiposity; reduced in adipocyte-specific Raptor-null mice, which are lean with enhanced mitochondrial respiration.

nodes.label: Food intake
nodes.description: Hypothalamic (arcuate nucleus) control of feeding; intracerebroventricular leucine and leptin suppress food intake through mTORC1, rapamycin abolishes that suppression, and rapamycin partially corrects the hyperphagic obesity of POMC-neuron Tsc1 deletion.

nodes.label: Hepatic steatosis
nodes.description: Hepatic triglyceride accumulation driven by SREBP1c lipogenesis under hyperinsulinaemia; paradoxically prevented by liver-specific Tsc1 deletion.

nodes.label: Hyperphagic obesity
nodes.description: Overeating with weight gain produced by Tsc1 deletion in POMC neurons and partially corrected by rapamycin; mechanistically expected in Smith-Kingsmore syndrome.

nodes.label: Hypertriglyceridaemia and hypercholesterolaemia
nodes.description: Dose-related elevation of triglycerides and cholesterol on mTOR inhibitors, reflecting altered hepatic and adipose lipid handling by both complexes.

nodes.label: Immunosenescence
nodes.description: Thymic involution, naive repertoire contraction, PD-1+ exhausted-like cells and inflammaging; the most productive clinical testing ground for geroprotection.

nodes.label: Peripheral insulin resistance
nodes.description: Reduced insulin-stimulated glucose disposal in peripheral tissues. Distinct from direct beta-cell toxicity: chronic mTORC2 loss produces peripheral insulin resistance, and the two mechanisms together account for rapamycin-associated new-onset diabetes at immunosuppressive exposures.

nodes.label: Interferon-stimulated antiviral gene expression
nodes.description: Upregulation of interferon-stimulated antiviral genes reported with RTB101 plus low-dose everolimus; the mechanistic correlate of the reduced laboratory-confirmed respiratory infections in that phase 2b.

nodes.label: Lean tissue mass
nodes.description: Fat-free body mass

nodes.label: Lifespan extension
nodes.description: Increase in median and maximal lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice given encapsulated rapamycin from 600 days of age, reproduced across three sites and dose- and sex-dependent.

nodes.label: Maladaptive cardiac remodelling
nodes.description: Pathological hypertrophic remodelling driven by sustained mTORC1 activity, distinct from the physiological hypertrophy that mTORC1 also supports; attenuated by partial inhibition in multiple models.

nodes.label: Amoeboid phagocytic microglial phenotype
nodes.description: Amoeboid, highly proliferative and phagocytic microglial state produced by Tsc1 loss, notably without a pro-inflammatory cytokine signature.

nodes.label: Denervation muscle atrophy
nodes.description: Loss of myofibre mass after denervation; prevented by constitutively active AKT, establishing sufficiency of the AKT-mTOR arm for maintenance of muscle mass.

nodes.label: Muscular dystrophy (Raptor-null)
nodes.description: Progressive dystrophy with impaired oxidative capacity and shortened lifespan after muscle-specific Raptor deletion; the phenotype against which near-silent Rictor deletion is contrasted.

nodes.label: Load-induced muscle hypertrophy
nodes.description: Hypertrophic growth of skeletal muscle in response to IGF-1, mechanical overload or chronic stimulation; mTORC1 is necessary and sufficient and rapamycin blocks it, which is the basis of the anabolic-resistance safety concern for chronic geroprotective dosing.

nodes.label: Myelination
nodes.description: Formation and thickness of myelin sheaths; requires oligodendrocyte mTORC1, with spinal cord affected more than corpus callosum.

nodes.label: Neurodegeneration
nodes.description: Progressive neuronal loss with ubiquitin-positive inclusions and motor deficits, produced by neural Atg5 or Atg7 deletion alone.

nodes.label: Oligodendrocyte differentiation
nodes.description: Maturation of oligodendrocyte precursors; impaired only in the Raptor/Rictor double mutant, indicating that mTORC2 contributes but is not rate-limiting while mTORC1 remains intact.

nodes.label: Osteoblast differentiation
nodes.description: Bone-forming cell differentiation requiring mTOR signalling.

nodes.label: Osteoclast differentiation
nodes.description: Bone-resorbing cell differentiation also requiring mTOR, which is why the net skeletal effect of inhibition is context-dependent.

nodes.label: PD-1+ CD4 and CD8 T cell fraction
nodes.description: Accumulation of PD-1-positive CD4 and CD8 T cells with age; fractions fell in older adults given low-dose everolimus before influenza vaccination.

nodes.label: Proteinuria
nodes.description: Urinary protein loss on mTOR inhibitors, reflecting the podocyte requirement for mTORC1 and disrupted podocyte autophagic flux.

nodes.label: Rapalog sensitivity
nodes.description: Tumour responsiveness to allosteric mTORC1 inhibition; predicted by proximal-brake lesions as enrichment rather than individual prediction, and not by distal-network lesions.

nodes.label: Sarcopenia
nodes.description: Age-related loss of muscle mass and function; the predicted consequence of chronic mTOR inhibition in skeletal muscle, and the central safety question for geroscience dosing.

nodes.label: Spontaneous recurrent seizures
nodes.description: Epileptic seizures; the shared endpoint of the mTORopathies and of microglial Tsc1 loss, with elevated SUDEP risk in GATOR1 epilepsies.

nodes.label: Dendritic spine density
nodes.description: Density of dendritic spines, which falls when forebrain mTORC2 activity and Tiam1–Rac1-dependent actin polymerisation are reduced.

nodes.label: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy
nodes.description: Elevated risk carried by the GATOR1-related familial focal epilepsies, which is part of why mTOR-directed therapy in this group is being pursued on limited evidence.

nodes.label: Th1 and Th17 differentiation
nodes.description: Effector CD4 lineages requiring Rheb-mTORC1; their suppression is part of the immunosuppressive action of rapalogs.

nodes.label: Regulatory T cell expansion
nodes.description: Preferential survival and expansion of CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ regulatory T cells under mTOR inhibition, while effector differentiation is blocked; the basis of the immunosuppressive use of rapamycin.

nodes.label: T-cell survival signalling
nodes.description: AKT-dependent survival output; the second mTORC2-dependent arm in T lymphocytes alongside Th2 differentiation.

nodes.label: Influenza vaccine antibody response
nodes.description: Placebo-corrected rise in haemagglutination-inhibition titre after influenza vaccination in adults aged 65 and over; the endpoint demonstrating an inverted-U dose-response to mTOR inhibition.

nodes.label: Adipose tissue
nodes.description: Tissue in which adipocyte Rictor deletion reduces insulin-stimulated glucose uptake, alters ChREBP-driven lipogenesis and lipid handling, and negatively controls whole-body growth.

nodes.label: Bone
nodes.description: Skeletal tissue; mTOR signalling is required for both osteoblast and osteoclast differentiation, so the net effect of inhibition is context-dependent.

nodes.label: Haematopoietic compartment
nodes.description: Marrow progenitor compartment whose proliferative mTORC1 requirement accounts for rapalog cytopenias; TSC-mTOR signalling also sets stem-cell quiescence.

nodes.label: Hypothalamic arcuate neuron
nodes.description: Arcuate neurons in which mTORC1 acts as a nutrient sensor rather than a growth regulator, integrating leucine and leptin into control of food intake.

nodes.label: Kidney podocyte
nodes.description: Glomerular epithelial cell with a calibrated Goldilocks requirement: both Tsc1 deletion and Raptor deletion produce injury and proteinuria.

nodes.label: Liver
nodes.description: Tissue in which the two complexes act in opposite directions on glucose output: mTORC1 drives SREBP1c lipogenesis while mTORC2 restrains gluconeogenesis through AKT–FOXO1.

nodes.label: Microglia
nodes.description: Resident CNS macrophage; Tsc1 deletion restricted to microglia produces an amoeboid proliferative phagocytic phenotype and severe early-onset seizures.

nodes.label: Oligodendrocyte
nodes.description: Oligodendrocyte-lineage cells of the CNS. Conditional deletion cleanly separates the two complexes: mTORC1 is rate-limiting for myelination, mTORC2 contributes but is not rate-limiting while mTORC1 remains intact. The requirement is regional, spinal cord being affected more than corpus callosum.

nodes.label: Oral epithelium
nodes.description: Rapidly renewing mucosal epithelium whose mTORC1 dependence accounts for rapalog stomatitis and the dose-limiting mucositis of bi-steric agents.

nodes.label: T lymphocyte
nodes.description: T lymphocyte compartment. The only tissue in which inhibition of the pathway produces the desired rather than an adverse effect: partial mTORC1 inhibition expands Tregs and enhances CD8 memory, which is the basis of rapalog immunosuppression and of the immune-function geroscience hypothesis.

nodes.label: Renal allograft rejection
nodes.description: Alloimmune destruction of a transplanted kidney; the first approved indication for sirolimus, given at continuous immunosuppressive exposures with trough monitoring.

nodes.label: New-onset diabetes after transplantation
nodes.description: Diabetes arising at immunosuppressive mTOR-inhibitor exposures; mechanistically beta-cell toxicity plus mTORC2-dependent peripheral insulin resistance

nodes.label: Brain amyloid-beta burden
nodes.description: Cerebral amyloid-beta accumulation, reduced by rapamycin in 3xTg-AD mice in an autophagy-dependent manner and largely only when treatment precedes substantial pathology.

nodes.label: Renal angiomyolipoma
nodes.description: TSC-associated renal tumour; 42% of patients achieved at least 50% reduction on everolimus (EXIST-2).

nodes.label: CNS drug exposure
nodes.description: Concentration of an mTOR inhibitor achieved in brain relative to blood; restricted and saturable for sirolimus and everolimus, so central and peripheral exposure-response relationships do not coincide.

nodes.label: Fatigue
nodes.description: Treatment-related fatigue, reported in 42% of patients in the RMC-5552 first-in-human dose-escalation study.

nodes.label: Hypercholesterolaemia
nodes.description: Elevated plasma cholesterol during mTOR-inhibitor therapy; occurs alongside hypertriglyceridaemia and is attributed to altered hepatic and adipose lipid handling (mTORC2 and mTORC1).

nodes.label: Hyperglycaemia
nodes.description: Elevated blood glucose on mTOR inhibitors, attributed chiefly to mTORC2 loss (peripheral insulin resistance) with a beta-cell contribution

nodes.label: Impaired wound healing
nodes.description: Delayed surgical healing and lymphocele formation on mTOR inhibitors, attributed to suppressed angiogenesis and fibroblast proliferation; managed by perioperative interruption.

nodes.label: Infection
nodes.description: Increased infection risk at immunosuppressive exposures, following from suppression of effector lymphocyte expansion; dose- and schedule-dependent and not seen consistently at low intermittent exposures.

nodes.label: Nausea
nodes.description: Treatment-related nausea, the second most frequent adverse event (44%) in the RMC-5552 first-in-human dose-escalation study.

nodes.label: Non-infectious pneumonitis
nodes.description: Non-infectious interstitial lung inflammation in roughly 5-15% of oncology patients receiving everolimus; the most serious and least mechanistically understood rapalog toxicity.

nodes.label: Misfolded protein aggregates
nodes.description: Aggregation-prone substrates cleared by macroautophagy (alpha-synuclein, polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin), reduced by rapamycin or temsirolimus in fly and mouse models.

nodes.label: Respiratory tract infection
nodes.description: Respiratory infections in older adults; ascertainment differs between participant-reported events in the phase 2a study and laboratory-confirmed events in phase 2b.

nodes.label: Subependymal giant cell astrocytoma
nodes.description: TSC-associated brain tumour; approximately 35% of patients achieved at least 50% volume reduction on everolimus versus 0% on placebo (EXIST-1).

nodes.label: Stomatitis / mucositis
nodes.description: Painful oral ulceration affecting roughly 30-60% of patients on rapalogs and 49% in the RMC-5552 phase 1 study; reflects mTORC1 dependence of renewing oral epithelium and is largely preventable.

nodes.label: Clinically symptomatic respiratory illness
nodes.description: Self-reported symptomatic respiratory illness; the subjective phase 3 endpoint that RTB101 monotherapy failed to meet in 1024 older adults.

edges.mechanism: Alpha-ketoglutarate promotes GTP loading of RagB and lysosomal translocation of mTORC1, reportedly through prolyl hydroxylase activity
edges.notes: The prolyl-hydroxylase requirement has been disputed and the hydroxylated target is not defined.

edges.mechanism: Amino-acid withdrawal recruits folliculin to lysosomes, where it binds RagA and is held in an inactive lysosomal complex; amino-acid restoration releases it and licenses RagC/D GTP hydrolysis, supporting Rag-dependent recruitment of mTORC1.
edges.notes: Lysosomal residence of FLCN rises when amino acids are withdrawn, whereas its RagC/D GAP activity is exerted when they are restored.

edges.mechanism: Amino-acid sufficiency promotes translocation of mTORC1 from a diffuse cytosolic pool to the lysosomal surface, where it encounters its proximate activator Rheb.GTP
Autophagy-derived amino acids reactivate mTORC1, so the autophagy-mTORC1 system oscillates rather than behaving as a switch
edges.notes: Kinetic consequence: readouts of autophagic flux depend strongly on sampling time after an intervention.

edges.mechanism: Luminal amino acids act through the v-ATPase, in a manner requiring its ATP hydrolysis, to weaken its interaction with Ragulator at the V1 sector without changing lysosomal pH; this conformational relay is the first step of inside-out signalling to the Rag GTPases.
Uncharged tRNAs accumulating during amino-acid deprivation bind the GCN2 HisRS-like domain, relieving autoinhibition and activating the kinase.
Arginine binds CASTOR1 with a dissociation constant of about 30 µM in a pocket at the interface of its ACT2 and ACT4 domains, triggering a conformational change that releases GATOR2.
edges.notes: The measured dissociation constant is about 30 µM (Chantranupong 2016).

edges.mechanism: Arginine binds the SLC38A9 transmembrane pocket; the cytosolic N terminus relays amino-acid availability to Rag-associated machinery.
sites: substrate pocket in the transmembrane bundle
edges.notes: The N-terminal signalling domain is distinct from the arginine-binding pocket.

edges.mechanism: Net effect of the SLC38A9-NPC1 signalling complex: lysosomal cholesterol sufficiency promotes mTORC1 activation independently of amino acids

SLC38A9 senses lysosomal cholesterol through conserved cholesterol-responsive motifs in its transmembrane region; this sterol input, separable from arginine sensing, drives Rag-dependent recruitment and activation of mTORC1.
edges.notes: The arginine-sensing and transport roles of SLC38A9 are well established, whereas the cholesterol arm is still emerging.

edges.mechanism: RagC/D must be GDP-loaded for the asymmetric, mTORC1-competent configuration; RagC.GTP yields the inactive heterodimer
RagD-GDP, generated by FLCN-FNIP GAP activity, is the configuration that together with RagA/B-GTP makes the heterodimer competent to recruit mTORC1
edges.notes: RagD is the RagC paralogue and carries the same GDP requirement.

edges.mechanism: Glutaminolysis converts glutamine via glutamate to alpha-ketoglutarate, the metabolite that links anaplerotic flux to Rag loading

Glutamine activates mTORC1 through an Arf1-dependent route that persists in RagA/B-deficient cells and requires the v-ATPase; this arm runs in parallel with Rag-dependent glutamine inputs such as glutaminolysis.
edges.notes: Reported by one laboratory lineage (Jewell 2015; Meng 2020) and not yet independently reproduced.

edges.mechanism: Glutamine supplies carbon, via glutamate and alpha-ketoglutarate, and nitrogen for TCA-cycle anaplerosis in proliferating cells.
GTP loading of RagA/B is the nucleotide state that confers Raptor binding on the heterodimer; the reciprocal state releases mTORC1 to the cytosol
GTP loading of RagB (the RagA paralogue) generates the signalling-competent RagB-GTP state that binds the Raptor claw
edges.notes: RagB is the RagA paralogue and carries the same GTP requirement.

edges.mechanism: Leucine allosterically activates glutamate dehydrogenase (GLUD1), increasing conversion of glutamate to alpha-ketoglutarate during glutaminolysis.
edges.notes: Classical allosteric regulation that also underlies leucine-stimulated insulin secretion; the link from alpha-ketoglutarate to Rag GTP loading rests on a single laboratory (Duran 2012).

edges.mechanism: Leucyl-tRNA synthetase was proposed to act as an intracellular leucine sensor, coupling leucine charging status to mTORC1
edges.notes: The model is contested: the yeast orthologue acts on the RagA/B counterpart with opposite polarity, and the two models have never been reconciled [51].

edges.mechanism: Leucine binds SAR1B and causes it to dissociate from GATOR2, relieving SAR1B-mediated inhibition of mTORC1; without leucine, SAR1B binds GATOR2 and inhibits mTORC1.
edges.notes: Single-laboratory finding awaiting independent replication.

edges.mechanism: Sestrin1 binds leucine to a similar extent as Sestrin2, through the C-terminal pocket conserved between them, and leucine releases endogenous Sestrin1 from GATOR2.
edges.notes: Sestrin3 binds leucine very weakly and its GATOR2 binding is leucine-insensitive (Wolfson 2016).

edges.mechanism: Free leucine binds Sestrin2 with a dissociation constant of approximately 20 uM through a C-terminal pocket, disrupting its grip on GATOR2
edges.notes: The binding is established in vitro and structurally, while its physiological primacy is contested.

edges.mechanism: Intracerebroventricular leucine raises hypothalamic S6K1 phosphorylation and suppresses food intake and body weight; rapamycin abolishes the effect.
edges.notes: Established in rodents; unresolved in humans, where no study has separated central from peripheral contributions.

edges.mechanism: The protein-feeding dose-response shifts rightward with age, so a per-meal leucine threshold of roughly 3-4 g is proposed to maximise synthesis in older adults.
edges.notes: The per-meal leucine threshold is a practical proposal rather than an established requirement; a systematic review of postprandial post-exercise muscle protein synthesis found leucine dose to predict the response in older adults without identifying a discrete threshold.

edges.mechanism: An oral bolus of roughly 3.4 g free leucine acutely stimulates human muscle protein synthesis and raises S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation, which remains elevated for about 90 minutes.
edges.context: human skeletal muscle, oral leucine bolus at rest

edges.mechanism: Methionine is converted to S-adenosylmethionine, so SAM concentration reports dietary methionine availability to the SAMTOR arm
edges.notes: Methionine is a well-established longevity-modifying nutrient, linked to mTORC1 by this route.

edges.mechanism: SAM binds SAMTOR with a Kd of approximately 7 uM; binding relieves SAMTOR-promoted GATOR1 activity

NPRL2 loss of function causes familial focal epilepsy of the GATOR1 spectrum through unopposed RagA/B-GTP loading and mTORC1 hyperactivity, with a focal cortical malformation in a minority of patients. In a small open-label series of NPRL2- and NPRL3-related epilepsy, add-on everolimus reduced seizures in all four patients treated, two of whom became seizure-free, although stomatitis led one patient to stop treatment.
edges.notes: The therapeutic evidence is open-label and very small; a controlled trial is required before mTOR inhibition becomes standard practice in these epilepsies.

edges.mechanism: Loss-of-function NPRL2 variants remove the catalytic arginine-finger subunit, abolishing GATOR1 GAP activity toward RagA/B.
Heterozygous NPRL2 loss impairs the GATOR1 GAP for RagA/B and raises mTORC1 activity.
GATOR1 loss (DEPDC5, NPRL2, NPRL3) belongs to the proximal-brake class and is somatic.
Testosterone/DHT bind the androgen receptor, driving its nuclear and non-genomic activity.
17β-estradiol binds ERα, enabling both genomic transcription and rapid non-genomic signalling to PI3K–AKT.
IGF-1 binding to IGF-1R induces β-subunit autophosphorylation and IRS/Shc docking; shares the IRS–PI3K–AKT route to TSC2/mTORC1 with insulin.
Chronic inflammatory signalling activates the IKK complex (IKKβ), which besides NF-κB engages TSC1; proposed link between inflammation and anabolic dysregulation of ageing tissue.
Insulin binds the INSR α-subunit ectodomain, triggering β-subunit trans-autophosphorylation and creating docking sites for IRS proteins and Shc.
Insulin and IGF-1 receptor engagement activates class I PI3K through IRS proteins, generating the PIP3 signal upstream of mTORC2.
The anorectic action of leptin requires intact hypothalamic mTOR signalling, making mTORC1 a nutrient and adiposity sensor rather than a growth regulator here.
The anorectic action of leptin requires intact hypothalamic mTOR signalling.
Eccentric contraction or stretch increases DGKζ-dependent PA synthesis; DGKζ overexpression is sufficient to induce fibre hypertrophy.

Mechanical stretch and eccentric contraction were reported to raise phosphatidic acid in skeletal muscle through phospholipase D, independently of ERK and PI3K; later work from the same laboratory found that phospholipase D activity does not rise with loading and that the mechanically induced phosphatidic acid depends on diacylglycerol kinase zeta.
edges.notes: The phospholipase D and diacylglycerol kinase zeta routes are competing accounts of the same load-induced rise in phosphatidic acid in skeletal muscle.

edges.mechanism: Eccentric contractions increase TSC2 RxRxxS/T-motif phosphorylation and move TSC2 away from the lysosome while mTOR associates with it; responsible kinase not defined.
edges.notes: The mechanistic link between mechanical load and TSC2 relocalisation rests on a single laboratory; phosphatidic acid/PLD and focal-adhesion routes are the alternatives [241,683].

edges.mechanism: Resistance exercise and mechanical overload activate mTORC1 in skeletal muscle, and rapamycin blocks the contraction-induced rise in human muscle protein synthesis. The proximal mechanism involves a rise in phosphatidic acid together with membrane perturbation and focal-adhesion signalling, but the enzyme generating that phosphatidic acid is disputed, with early work implicating phospholipase D and later work diacylglycerol kinase zeta.
edges.notes: The net activation of mTORC1 by loading is reproducible while the proximal lipid step is unsettled; opposite in sign to the endurance-exercise input to AMPK, so exercise modality determines the net effect.

edges.mechanism: TNF-alpha engagement of TNFR1 activates the IKK complex, including IKK-beta, through the receptor-proximal adaptors TRADD, TRAF2 and TAK1; the relationship is indirect rather than a direct contact between TNF-alpha and IKK-beta.
Biallelic truncating TBC1D7 variants destabilise the TSC complex and increase mTORC1 activity, causing macrocephaly/megalencephaly with intellectual disability.
edges.notes: Two independent families

edges.mechanism: Canonical Wnt signalling (Dishevelled/LRP6–Axin) inhibits GSK3, preventing TSC2 Ser1337/1341 phosphorylation and thereby activating mTORC1 independently of β-catenin.
A-769662 binds the ADaM site between the alpha kinase domain and beta1 carbohydrate-binding module, allosterically activating AMPK and protecting pThr172; beta1-selective, no AMP mimicry.
edges.notes: Prototype of ADaM-site activators (MK-8722, PF-739).

edges.mechanism: ADP binds the AMPK gamma-subunit nucleotide sites and protects phospho-Thr172 from dephosphorylation without causing allosteric activation.
edges.notes: Several laboratories have reproduced ADP protection of Thr172, but ADP is about ten-fold less potent than AMP. Whether ADP also promotes Thr172 phosphorylation, and whether it contributes substantially to AMPK activation in vivo, is disputed.

edges.mechanism: AICAR is taken up and phosphorylated to ZMP, an AMP mimetic that binds the AMPK gamma subunit, allosterically activating AMPK and promoting Thr172 phosphorylation; has AMPK-independent effects.
AMP binds CBS sites 1 and 3 of the gamma subunit, allosterically activating AMPK (2-5 fold), promoting Thr172 phosphorylation by LKB1 and protecting pThr172 from phosphatases.
Mg-free ATP competes with AMP/ADP for the gamma-subunit CBS sites; at high energy charge ATP occupancy keeps AMPK in the inactive, phosphatase-accessible state.
Ca2+/calmodulin binding relieves CaMKK2 autoinhibition, enabling it to phosphorylate AMPK (and CaMKI/IV).
Local lysosomal Ca2+ binds calmodulin and activates calcineurin adjacent to the lysosomal surface

Reduced energy intake lowers cellular energy charge and insulin, reported to increase AMPK activity in liver and muscle, converging with metformin and exercise on the AMPK-TSC2/Raptor brake on mTORC1.
edges.context: liver, skeletal muscle; rodent CR regimens
edges.notes: Caloric restriction is held to converge on AMPK, but direct in vivo evidence of AMPK activation by caloric restriction is inconsistent across tissues and protocols.

edges.mechanism: Restricted feeding is the dominant entraining cue for peripheral oscillators, shifting the phase of hepatic circadian gene expression by up to twelve hours while leaving the suprachiasmatic clock unchanged, and caloric restriction likewise reprograms hepatic clock gene expression.

Caloric restriction lowers hepatic mTORC1 activity at some times of day while having no effect, or the opposite effect, at others, so the measured response depends on when liver is sampled relative to the feeding schedule.
edges.notes: Based on a single study sampling mouse liver at six times across the day; dietary-restriction studies using different feeding schedules are therefore not directly comparable.

edges.mechanism: DNA double-strand breaks recruit MRN, which activates ATM by intermolecular autophosphorylation (Ser1981) and dimer dissociation.

Genotoxic stress activates ATM/ATR and CHK2, which phosphorylate p53 at Ser15 and Ser20, weakening MDM2 binding and stabilising p53; p53 then induces mTORC1-suppressing target genes, including SESN1 and SESN2.
edges.notes: support comes from the primary p53 literature.

edges.mechanism: When ATP consumption exceeds production, adenylate kinase (2 ADP <-> ATP + AMP) amplifies the AMP rise so AMP:ATP changes roughly as the square of ADP:ATP, making AMP the sensitive low-energy signal.
Energy stress (rising AMP/ADP:ATP) activates AMPK through gamma-subunit nucleotide binding and LKB1-dependent Thr172 phosphorylation; AMPK then inhibits mTORC1 via TSC2 and Raptor.
Energy stress (2-deoxyglucose, glucose deprivation) induces REDD1 through ATF4; REDD1 is required for mTORC1 inhibition in this setting, partly independently of AMPK.
Unfolded-protein load releases BiP/GRP78 from the PERK luminal domain; PERK dimerises and autophosphorylates, launching the integrated stress response.
Contractile activity raises AMP/ADP:ATP and creatine/phosphocreatine turnover in muscle fibres, increasing LKB1-dependent AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation in an intensity-dependent manner.

Muscle contraction consumes ATP faster than oxidative phosphorylation replenishes it, so ADP and, through adenylate kinase, AMP rise, and this energy-stress state activates AMPK in proportion to exercise intensity.
edges.notes: Exercise converges on AMPK through the contraction-induced shift in adenylate charge.

edges.mechanism: FBP occupancy of aldolase prevents the apo-aldolase conformation; on glucose withdrawal FBP falls, apo-aldolase forms and nucleates the lysosomal v-ATPase–Ragulator–AXIN–LKB1 platform that activates AMPK before any measurable change in the AMP:ATP ratio.

Glucose starvation induces OGT-dependent O-GlcNAcylation of LARS1 at Ser1042, which blocks LARS1 binding to RagD and promotes ULK1 phosphorylation of its leucine-binding site, so LARS1 relays leucine to mTORC1 only when glucose is available.
Glycolytic flux converts glucose to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate, so FBP concentration tracks glucose availability and serves as the proximal signal in the aldolase-dependent glucose-sensing route.

Glucose sufficiency is relayed to mTORC1 through the Rag GTPases largely independently of AMPK (constitutively active RagA mice lose glucose sensing); glycolytic DHAP has been proposed as the sensed metabolite.
edges.notes: The direct glucose/DHAP sensor upstream of the Rags is unknown.

edges.mechanism: Glucose supplies carbon for glycolysis after phosphorylation to glucose-6-phosphate.

Withdrawal of glucose activates AMPK through LKB1-dependent phosphorylation of Thr172: the canonical route follows the fall in ATP and the rise in AMP and ADP, while a parallel route in which unoccupied aldolase senses the loss of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate has been reported to act before adenine nucleotide ratios change.
edges.notes: The aldolase route is reported by a single laboratory, whereas activation of AMPK by glucose withdrawal itself is reproduced widely.

edges.mechanism: Glucose withdrawal suppresses mTORC1 even in AMPK-null cells, so an AMPK-independent arm operates in parallel with the LKB1-AMPK route; the proposed effectors, Rag-GTPase-dependent release of mTORC1 from the lysosome and hexokinase-II binding to Raptor, each rest on a single report.
edges.notes: The existence of an AMPK-independent arm is well supported; the molecular identity of that arm is not.

edges.mechanism: Glucose withdrawal shifts the Rag heterodimer to its inactive nucleotide state, releasing mTORC1 from the lysosomal surface; mice expressing GTP-locked RagA cannot execute this switch and die of neonatal glucose-starvation failure.
edges.notes: The in vivo genetic evidence comes from mice expressing GTP-locked RagA, which cannot inactivate the heterodimer and die of neonatal starvation.

edges.mechanism: The carbohydrate-binding module of the AMPK β-subunit binds glycogen, and branched glycogen with exposed α-1,6 branch points inhibits AMPK activity and Thr172 phosphorylation, so cellular carbohydrate reserves restrain the energy-stress arm independently of the AMP:ATP ratio.
edges.notes: Glycogen reserves restrain AMPK independently of the AMP:ATP ratio, which is why glycogen depletion is a determinant of AMPK activation during exercise.

edges.mechanism: Limited oxidative phosphorylation lowers ATP and raises AMP/ADP, activating LKB1-AMPK, which phosphorylates TSC2 and Raptor; a REDD1-independent arm of hypoxic mTORC1 inhibition.
edges.notes: the REDD1-TSC route acts without AMPK or LKB1. Mitochondrial ROS have also been proposed to activate AMPK in hypoxia independently of the AMP:ATP ratio.

edges.mechanism: Hypoxia induces REDD1 (via HIF-1 and, under severe hypoxia/ER stress, ATF4); REDD1 is required for hypoxic mTORC1 inhibition, which is lost in REDD1-/- and TSC2-/- cells.

Falling O2 tension limits the prolyl-hydroxylase reaction, inactivating PHD2 and allowing HIF-1α to escape hydroxylation and degradation; this is the molecular basis of the HIF-1α stabilisation that drives REDD1 and BNIP3 induction.
Low O2 blocks PHD-mediated prolyl hydroxylation of HIF-1alpha; VHL no longer binds, ubiquitination ceases and HIF-1alpha accumulates to drive hypoxia-responsive genes including DDIT4 and BNIP3.
edges.notes: HIF-1alpha is itself a translational output of mTORC1, so hypoxic signalling through HIF-1alpha closes a feedback loop onto the pathway.

edges.mechanism: Hypoxia suppresses mTORC1 by two indirect routes: HIF-1alpha-dependent induction of REDD1 with consequent TSC activation, which proceeds without AMPK or LKB1, and, when hypoxia is severe enough to lower ATP, activation of AMPK.
edges.notes: A summary of two indirect routes rather than a direct interaction.

edges.mechanism: H2O2/mitochondrial ROS increase AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation; proposed direct oxidation of AMPK alpha Cys299/Cys304 versus indirect activation through ATP depletion and AMP/ADP rise.
edges.notes: Direct redox activation at AMPK alpha Cys299/Cys304 is disputed; the opposing account holds that mitochondria-derived reactive oxygen species act indirectly through the cellular energy state.

edges.mechanism: H2O2 oxidises ATM Cys2991, forming disulfide-linked active dimers independently of DNA breaks and MRN; this cytoplasmic ATM pool drives the LKB1-AMPK-TSC2 response to ROS.
ROS act on a peroxisome-localised TSC1-TSC2 pool, activating TSC2 GAP activity to suppress Rheb-GTP and mTORC1 and to induce autophagy (pexophagy).

Autosomal recessive STRADA loss causes polyhydramnios, megalencephaly and symptomatic (intractable) epilepsy through impaired LKB1-AMPK signalling and mTORC1 hyperactivation; rapamycin reduces seizures.
edges.notes: Rapamycin efficacy in PMSE rests on preclinical work together with small clinical studies.

edges.mechanism: Autosomal recessive STRADA loss impairs LKB1-AMPK signalling and causes PMSE syndrome with megalencephaly and intractable epilepsy.
edges.notes: Rapamycin supported by preclinical and small clinical evidence.

edges.mechanism: Biallelic STRADA loss removes the pseudokinase subunit required for LKB1 activity and cytoplasmic localisation, so the LKB1–STRADα–MO25 heterotrimer cannot assemble and LKB1–AMPK signalling is impaired.
edges.notes: Impaired LKB1-AMPK signalling is the complex-level consequence of losing the pseudokinase subunit.

edges.mechanism: Loss of LKB1-AMPK restraint in STRADA-null neurons produces constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivity, the shared mechanism of the mTORopathies; rapamycin rescues aberrant cortical lamination and heterotopia in STRADA-depleted preclinical models, and the human experience is a small open-label series reporting reduced seizure frequency.
edges.notes: Evidence for benefit in affected patients is preclinical together with a small uncontrolled series, not a controlled trial.

edges.mechanism: Biallelic STRADA (LYK5) deletion removes the LKB1 pseudokinase activator; LKB1 is mislocalised/inactive, AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation falls and neuronal mTORC1 becomes hyperactive.
Biallelic STRADA loss impairs LKB1-AMPK signalling, removing energy-stress restraint of mTORC1 in PMSE syndrome.

Lysosomal stress, including oxidative stress sensed directly by TRPML1 (MCOLN1), opens this lysosomal Ca2+ channel; the released Ca2+ activates calcineurin, which dephosphorylates TFEB and drives its nuclear translocation independently of mTORC1 inhibition.
Light drives mTORC1-dependent inhibitory phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 in the SCN, releasing eIF4E and de-repressing translation of Vip and other mRNAs required for entrainment
Photic input to SCN neurons activates the MEK–ERK cascade during the phase-shifting window, the proximal step preceding mTORC1 activation
Light activates MNK1 via ERK in SCN neurons, linking photic input to eIF4E phosphorylation
Photic stimulation during the subjective night acutely raises mTORC1 pathway activity in SCN neurons (increased phospho-S6K1 and phospho-4E-BP1), gating the translational response to light.
edges.context: mouse SCN, light pulse during subjective night

edges.mechanism: Sleep loss increases 4E-BP2-mediated repression of cap-dependent translation in hippocampal neurons; restoring translation initiation rescues the memory deficit
edges.notes: PMID 27117251: Tudor JC et al., Sci Signal 2016;9(425):ra41.

edges.mechanism: Acute sleep deprivation suppresses mTORC1-dependent signalling in hippocampus, reducing cap-dependent protein synthesis required for memory consolidation
edges.notes: The documented sleep-to-mTOR arm. PMID 27117251: Tudor JC et al., Sci Signal 2016;9(425):ra41.

edges.mechanism: Loss of BMAL1 removes the S6K1-phosphorylated BMAL1 species from the translation-initiation machinery, reducing cap-dependent protein synthesis and abolishing its diurnal rhythm
Germline Bmal1 deletion removes the clock-dependent restraint on mTORC1, producing constitutively increased mTORC1 signalling across tissues.
Halving Bmal1 gene dosage rescues the circadian behavioural abnormalities caused by mTOR hyperactivation, indicating that excess rather than deficient BMAL1 protein mediates them.
edges.context: heterozygous Bmal1 reduction on a Tsc2-heterozygous, mTOR-hyperactive background
edges.notes: The published manipulation is a partial reduction of BMAL1; complete loss of BMAL1 abolishes behavioural rhythmicity rather than normalising it.

edges.mechanism: Bmal1-null mice develop premature ageing phenotypes attributed in part to the unrestrained mTORC1 signalling that accompanies loss of the clock's positive limb.
Bmal1-null tissues show constitutively elevated mTORC1 output, read out as increased S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation and downstream S6 phosphorylation
edges.notes: Increased mTORC1 activity; the readout is S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation as measured in the primary study [304].

edges.mechanism: Loss of PER2 removes the TSC1-delivery mechanism, elevating mTORC1 activity and flattening its time-of-day dependence
Age-associated elevation of basal mTOR activity with impaired stress-responsive autophagy contributes to accumulation of misfolded aggregates.

The acute mTORC1 response of aged muscle to amino acids and to loading is attenuated; basal post-absorptive signalling has been reported as elevated in some studies and unchanged in others, so the dynamic range appears compressed rather than uniformly reduced.
edges.notes: Central to the safety argument against indiscriminate mTOR inhibition in older adults.

edges.mechanism: Ageing muscle shows a blunted protein-synthesis response to amino acids and loading, from reduced mTORC1 sensitivity, impaired perfusion and splanchnic extraction.
Ageing produces thymic involution, contraction of the naive repertoire, accumulation of PD-1+ exhausted-like cells and the low-grade inflammation of inflammaging.
Age-associated decline in immune function is the premise of the three trials that define the geroprotective evidence base.
Resistance exercise activates mTORC1 through phospholipase D-derived phosphatidic acid, mechanically induced membrane perturbation and focal adhesion signalling.

Pharmacological activation of mTORC2 with A-443654 raises hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation of its substrates in mouse and fly; the compound is not selective for mTORC2, and no directly acting, selective mTORC2 agonist has been independently validated.
Raising mTORC2 activity enhances L-LTP and long-term memory in wild-type animals and reverses age-associated memory impairment in both mice and flies.
Distal-network lesions do not predict rapalog benefit: BOLERO-2 benefit was independent of PIK3CA genotype, while selection succeeded at PI3K (SOLAR-1) and AKT (CAPItello-291).
edges.notes: Established that benefit is genotype-independent; contested as to mechanism.

edges.mechanism: Proximal-brake lesions identify a population enriched for mTORC1 dependency: exceptional responders in urothelial and renal carcinoma, but a negative prospective basket study.
edges.notes: Necessary rather than sufficient; as a basis for routine biomarker selection, contested.

edges.mechanism: Truncating and missense DEPDC5 variants disrupt the Rag-binding subunit of GATOR1, so the complex can no longer be recruited to and act on RagA/B; missense variants are often hypomorphic rather than null.

Germline heterozygous DEPDC5 loss of function disinhibits RagA/B and produces mTORC1 hyperactivity in the cortical lesion, causing familial focal epilepsy with variable foci and elevated risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy.
edges.notes: In a small open-label series, the three patients with DEPDC5 truncating variants had the largest seizure reductions on everolimus while the patient with a missense variant responded less; the evidence is open-label and very small.

edges.mechanism: Heterozygous DEPDC5 loss reduces GATOR1 GAP activity toward RagA/B, so mTORC1 remains lysosomally recruited when amino acids are scarce.

In an open-label series of five patients treated with everolimus titrated to troughs of 5-15 ng/mL, the three with DEPDC5 loss-of-function variants showed substantial seizure reduction, while a DEPDC5 missense variant gave a smaller response.
edges.notes: Genotype within GATOR1 appears to predict response; the evidence is emerging, in contrast to the established case of everolimus in TSC.

edges.mechanism: GATOR1 component loss removes a direct restraint on mTORC1 recruitment and so belongs to the proximal-brake class.

Genotype within the GATOR1 complex appears to influence everolimus response in the familial focal epilepsies: in an open-label series, patients with DEPDC5 loss-of-function variants showed substantial seizure reduction, a patient with a DEPDC5 missense variant responded less, and the single NPRL3 patient worsened, whereas a later series in NPRL2- and NPRL3-related epilepsy reported seizure reduction in all four treated patients. The evidence is open-label and very small, and a controlled trial is required before this becomes practice.
Germline MTOR gain-of-function causes Smith-Kingsmore syndrome with macrocephaly, intellectual disability and seizures; E1799K accounts for roughly half of cases.

The recurrent germline E1799K substitution increases mTOR kinase activity, with raised mTOR signalling in patient-derived cells that is suppressed by rapamycin; it is the most common variant in Smith-Kingsmore syndrome, accounting for roughly half of reported cases.
Germline activating MTOR substitutions cause Smith–Kingsmore syndrome; the recurrent E1799K change accounts for roughly half of reported cases.

Germline gain-of-function MTOR variants (E1799K accounting for roughly half of cases) hyperactivate mTORC1, the proximate cause of both the somatic and the circadian features of Smith–Kingsmore syndrome
SKS-associated MTOR variants reduced circadian reporter amplitude in engineered U2OS cells.
Somatic mosaic activating MTOR variants confined to the malformed cortex cause focal cortical dysplasia type II with drug-resistant focal epilepsy.
edges.context: somatic mosaicism restricted to dysplastic cortex
edges.notes: Management is surgical; mTOR inhibition remains investigational.

edges.mechanism: Somatic mosaic MTOR activation also causes hemimegalencephaly, the more severe end of the same mosaic malformation spectrum as FCD type II.
Somatic mosaic activating MTOR variants confined to malformed cortex raise kinase activity in the affected cell lineage only.
Activating MTOR variants act at the kinase itself. Depending on the variant, they can enhance mTORC1 and/or mTORC2 outputs.
edges.notes: Proximity to mTOR does not by itself establish tumour dependence or predict response to rapalogs.

edges.mechanism: Activating FAT- and kinase-domain MTOR variants raise kinase activity two- to ten-fold and were present in exceptional responders, including concurrent E2014K and E2419K in a urothelial complete responder treated with everolimus and pazopanib.
edges.notes: No genomic biomarker of rapalog response has been prospectively validated.

edges.mechanism: NPRL3 loss of function causes familial focal epilepsy of the GATOR1 spectrum through unopposed RagA/B-GTP loading and mTORC1 hyperactivity in the cortical lesion. Responses to add-on everolimus have differed between series: the single NPRL3 patient in the first case series worsened, whereas all four patients in a later NPRL2- and NPRL3-related series improved, two of them becoming seizure-free.
edges.notes: The small open-label series do not establish NPRL3 genotype as a predictor of everolimus failure, and a controlled trial is required before mTOR inhibition becomes standard practice.

edges.mechanism: Loss-of-function NPRL3 variants destabilise the GATOR1 heterotrimer and abolish its GAP activity toward RagA/B.
Heterozygous NPRL3 loss impairs the GATOR1 GAP for RagA/B and raises mTORC1 activity.
One NPRL3 participant worsened in the 2023 series; the 2025 NPRL2/NPRL3 series instead reported improvement in all four participants.
edges.notes: Small uncontrolled samples do not establish a genotype-specific response rule.

edges.mechanism: GATOR1 loss (DEPDC5, NPRL2, NPRL3) belongs to the proximal-brake class and is somatic.

Loss-of-function STK11/LKB1 lesions abolish energy-stress-induced Thr172 phosphorylation of AMPK, removing both the TSC2-GAP and the Raptor Ser792 brakes, so mTORC1 is no longer restrained when ATP falls; Ca2+-driven Thr172 phosphorylation by CaMKK2 is retained, and growth-factor and amino-acid control of mTORC1 persists.
edges.notes: A single-arm trial of everolimus in advanced solid tumours selected for TSC1, TSC2, NF1, NF2 or STK11 mutations showed no meaningful single-agent activity, so such a lesion marks an enriched population rather than demonstrated dependence on the kinase.

edges.mechanism: Germline (Peutz-Jeghers) or somatic STK11 inactivation abolishes AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation under energy stress; the TSC2/Raptor checkpoints fail and mTORC1 is deregulated in LKB1-null cells and tumours.
LKB1 loss removes the principal activating kinase of AMPK, withdrawing AMPK-mediated restraint of mTORC1 via TSC2 and Raptor Ser792.
Loss of STK11 is listed among the recurrent alterations in the pathway landscape, and STK11 was one of the five selection genes in the negative prospective everolimus basket study.
Germline STK11 (LKB1) loss causes Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, with hamartomatous polyposis attributable in part to withdrawn AMPK restraint of mTORC1.
edges.notes: Supported by the primary literature. STK11 loss of function also occurs as a somatic cancer lesion.

edges.mechanism: TSC1 loss destabilises TSC2 and abolishes Rheb-GAP activity → constitutive mTORC1 activation; basis of tuberous sclerosis; proximal-brake lesion predicting rapalog sensitivity.
edges.context: tuberous sclerosis; urothelial carcinoma exceptional responders

edges.mechanism: Loss of the TSC complex removes GAP activity toward Rheb, producing the constitutive mTOR hyperactivation of the paradigmatic genetic mTORopathy model used to study BMAL1 proteostasis
mTOR hyperactivation in the TSC-null model produces circadian behavioural abnormalities that are rescued by reducing Bmal1 gene dosage
Podocyte Tsc1 deletion produces focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, the upper limb of the podocyte Goldilocks requirement for calibrated mTORC1 activity.
Germline TSC1 loss with a somatic second hit produces constitutive mTORC1 activation in lesional tissue: cortical tubers, SEGA, angiomyolipoma and epilepsy.
Whole-genome sequencing of a durable everolimus complete responder found loss-of-function TSC1; TSC1 mutations occurred in roughly 8% of 109 further bladder cancers.
edges.notes: Correlated with everolimus sensitivity and time on treatment.

edges.mechanism: Liver-specific Tsc1 deletion constitutively activates mTORC1 yet protects against diet-induced steatosis, because S6K1-IRS-1 feedback suppresses hepatic insulin signalling and SREBP1c.
Tsc1 deletion in POMC neurons produces hyperphagic obesity, the converse manipulation to hypothalamic leucine sensing.

Whole-genome sequencing of a durable complete responder to everolimus identified a loss-of-function TSC1 mutation; TSC1 mutations were then found in approximately 8% of a further 109 bladder cancers and correlated with everolimus sensitivity and time on treatment.
edges.notes: This is enrichment rather than prediction: a proximal-brake lesion is necessary but not sufficient for rapalog sensitivity.

edges.mechanism: Tsc1 deletion restricted to microglia produces severe early-onset spontaneous recurrent seizures, showing epileptogenesis is not cell-autonomous to neurons.
edges.notes: If a glial compartment contributes, the cell type in which a drug engages target may determine efficacy.

edges.mechanism: TSC1 loss destabilises the TSC complex and abolishes TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb, so Rheb-GTP accumulates and mTORC1 is constitutively activated.
edges.context: germline plus somatic second hit, or somatic

edges.mechanism: TSC1 loss impairs the TSC complex and releases Rheb-dependent mTORC1 signalling.
edges.notes: This classification does not establish mTORC1 as the only affected process or guarantee treatment response.

edges.mechanism: TSC1 loss of function was identified in an exceptional everolimus responder and correlated with sensitivity and time on treatment in 109 further bladder cancers; prospective basket testing was negative.
edges.context: urothelial carcinoma outside tuberous sclerosis complex
edges.notes: A proximal-brake lesion is better described as necessary than sufficient for rapalog response.

edges.mechanism: TSC2 loss abolishes the asparagine-thumb GAP activity toward Rheb → constitutive mTORC1 activation; basis of TSC, LAM and PEComa (AMPECT response enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours).
edges.notes: AMPECT enrichment [633].

edges.mechanism: TSC1 and TSC2 act alongside MTOR, PIK3CA and AKT3 in focal cortical dysplasia type II, through somatic mosaic activation confined to the malformed cortex.
TSC2-deficient smooth-muscle-like cells with constitutive mTORC1 activity drive the cystic lung destruction of LAM, sporadic or TSC-associated.
edges.notes: LAM is a feature of TSC and sirolimus is approved for it; the lesion-to-LAM link comes from the primary literature.

edges.mechanism: Germline TSC2 loss of function with a somatic second hit abolishes TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb, producing constitutive mTORC1 activation in lesional tissue, the molecular basis of tuberous sclerosis complex.
Tsc2 acts as a molecular checkpoint controlling osteoblast development and glucose homeostasis.
In AMPECT, response to nab-sirolimus in malignant PEComa was enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours.
TSC2 loss removes the asparagine-thumb GAP that accelerates Rheb GTP hydrolysis roughly 100-fold, producing constitutive Rheb-GTP and mTORC1 activation.
edges.context: germline plus somatic second hit, or somatic

edges.mechanism: TSC2 loss removes the Rheb GTPase-activating function that normally restrains mTORC1.
edges.notes: Clinical response depends on disease and treatment context.

edges.mechanism: Response to albumin-bound sirolimus in malignant PEComa was strongly enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours, the clearest somatic example of a proximal-brake lesion enriching for rapalog benefit without establishing dependency in an individual tumour.
p110α-selective ATP-competitive inhibitor; with fulvestrant improved PFS from 5.7 to 11.0 months in PIK3CA-mutant HR+ advanced breast cancer (SOLAR-1).
PI3K-alpha-selective inhibitor used in SOLAR-1.
Alpelisib selectively inhibits the p110-alpha catalytic subunit at the ATP site, lowering PIP3 and hence AKT and downstream mTORC1 activation.
SOLAR-1 added alpelisib to fulvestrant and improved PFS from 5.7 to 11.0 months in a population prospectively selected for PIK3CA mutation: genomic selection succeeds at the PI3K node.
Added to fulvestrant in a population prospectively selected for PIK3CA mutation, alpelisib improved progression-free survival from 5.7 to 11.0 months: biomarker selection succeeds at the PI3K node.
Apitolisib inhibits mTOR at the ATP site alongside class I PI3K, abolishing output of both complexes.

Class I PI3K inhibition lowers PIP3 and therefore both AKT recruitment and mSin1-dependent mTORC2 activation. In a randomised comparison with everolimus in renal cell carcinoma, apitolisib produced shorter progression-free survival and markedly more high-grade hyperglycaemia and rash, illustrating the toxicity ceiling that limited dual PI3K-mTOR inhibitors developed to pre-empt feedback reactivation.
AZD8055 reduces phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 at Thr37/Thr46, thereby favouring its repressive interaction with eIF4E.
edges.notes: Indirect activation of the translational repressor through reduced mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation; the drug does not directly activate 4E-BP1.

edges.mechanism: AZD8055 is a potent, selective, orally bioavailable ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor active against both complexes, with antitumour activity in vitro and in vivo.
ATP-competitive occupancy of the catalytic cleft inhibits mTORC2 as well as mTORC1, abolishing AKT Ser473 phosphorylation.
Pan-AKT ATP-competitive inhibitor; with fulvestrant improved PFS from 3.1 to 7.3 months in AKT-pathway-altered HR+ breast cancer (CAPItello-291).
ATP-competitive pan-AKT inhibitor used in CAPItello-291.
Capivasertib is an ATP-competitive pan-AKT inhibitor, blocking both the mTORC1-directed arm (through TSC2 and PRAS40) and the mTORC1-independent outputs to GSK3-beta, FOXO and MDM2.
CAPItello-291 added capivasertib to fulvestrant and improved PFS from 3.1 to 7.3 months in tumours with AKT-pathway alterations: genomic selection also succeeds at the AKT node.
