FKBP12, a peptidyl-prolyl isomerase, is the intracellular receptor for rapamycin and contributes one half of the composite surface that binds FRB. Inhibition of mTOR is a gain of function of the drug-immunophilin complex, not a consequence of blocking isomerase activity.

The composite FKBP12-rapamycin surface wedges into the FRB domain adjacent to the catalytic cleft, narrowing substrate access; this gain-of-function mechanism explains why rapamycin is an allosteric, substrate-selective inhibitor rather than an ATP-competitive one.
The FKBP12-rapamycin binary complex engages the four-helix FRB bundle, forming the ternary complex resolved crystallographically.
The ternary structure shows the drug sandwiched between FKBP12 and a hydrophobic FRB cleft; neither protein contacts the other substantially, so binding is strictly drug-dependent.
edges.notes: Ternary complex structure: Choi 1996, reference [108].

edges.mechanism: With prolonged exposure the drug-immunophilin complex captures newly synthesised mTOR before it is incorporated into mTORC2, depleting the complex rather than inhibiting the assembled one.
edges.notes: Kinetic, not structural, selectivity: acute experiments and chronic dosing study different pharmacology.

edges.mechanism: Docking on the exposed FRB of assembled mTORC1 sterically restricts access of substrates to the already deep catalytic cleft rather than abolishing catalysis, giving partial, substrate-selective inhibition.
The cyclosporine-cyclophilin A complex binds and inhibits calcineurin, converging on the same target as the tacrolimus-FKBP12 complex; neither free immunophilin inhibits the phosphatase.
Arf1 is required for glutamine-induced mTORC1 activation and lysosomal translocation by a route that does not require the Rag GTPases
edges.notes: The Arf1-dependent, Rag-independent glutamine route has been reported by one laboratory lineage (Jewell 2015; Meng 2020) and has not been independently reproduced.

edges.mechanism: C12orf66 is one of the four subunits of the KICSTOR scaffold
DEPDC5 is the largest of the three GATOR1 subunits and provides the principal Rag-binding surface

DEPDC5 binds GTP-loaded RagA with high affinity in an inhibitory mode that restrains, rather than stimulates, GATOR1-mediated GTP hydrolysis; catalysis is executed through weaker NPRL2-NPRL3 contacts, and the DEPDC5 mode is proposed to keep GATOR1 from becoming hyperactive.
edges.notes: DEPDC5 is the main Rag-binding subunit of GATOR1 but not its catalytic subunit; the role of the inhibitory binding mode in cells is still being defined.

edges.mechanism: Folliculin supplies the longin GAP domain of the FLCN-FNIP heterodimer
FLCN-FNIP is the GAP for RagC, driving it to the GDP state required for the active heterodimer; unlike GATOR1 this GAP activity is positive for mTORC1
FLCN-FNIP acts with the same polarity on RagD, the RagC paralogue, promoting the GDP state that supports mTORC1 recruitment

FLCN-FNIP loads RagC/D with GDP, which is specifically required for mTORC1 to phosphorylate TFEB at Ser211 and keep it cytoplasmic; FLCN loss therefore leaves TFEB nuclear while S6K1 and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation are preserved.
edges.notes: The effect on TFEB is indirect, exerted through the Rag heterodimer, and explains the tissue-dependent rather than uniform mTORC1 phenotype of FLCN loss.

edges.mechanism: FNIP1 was identified through its interaction with both folliculin and AMPK, suggesting the FLCN-FNIP module also reads energy status
edges.notes: The functional consequence of the FNIP1-AMPK interaction is not settled.

edges.mechanism: FNIP1 heterodimerises with folliculin to form the catalytically competent RagC/D GAP
FNIP2 is the paralogue of FNIP1 and forms an equivalent FLCN-FNIP2 GAP complex
GATOR1 is the GTPase-activating protein for RagA, driving GTP hydrolysis and so releasing mTORC1 from the lysosome; it is active when amino acids are scarce
GATOR1 acts with equivalent GAP polarity on RagB, the RagA paralogue, making it a negative regulator of mTORC1 recruitment
GATOR2 is a positive regulator of mTORC1 that acts by inhibiting GATOR1; the molecular basis of that inhibition remains incompletely defined
edges.notes: The mechanism by which GATOR2 inhibits GATOR1 is not fully resolved.

edges.mechanism: ITFG2 is one of the four subunits of the KICSTOR scaffold
KICSTOR recruits GATOR1 to the lysosomal surface; without it GATOR1 cannot reach its Rag substrate and nutrients fail to regulate mTORC1
The KICSTOR scaffold localises to the lysosomal surface and is the platform that positions GATOR1 there
KPTN is one of the four subunits of the KICSTOR scaffold
N-terminal myristoylation and palmitoylation of LAMTOR1 anchor Ragulator, and with it the Rag heterodimer, to the lysosomal membrane
edges.notes: LAMTOR1 is lipid-anchored; the specific modified residues are reported in the primary literature.

edges.mechanism: LAMTOR1 wraps around the LAMTOR2-5 roadblock heterodimers and supplies the membrane anchor of the pentameric complex

LAMTOR1 (p18) binds the v-ATPase directly, contacting V0 subunit d1 and V1 subunit D, and so physically couples the proton pump to the Ragulator-Rag module; amino acids weaken the Ragulator interaction with the V1 sector.
LAMTOR2 forms a roadblock heterodimer with LAMTOR3 within Ragulator
LAMTOR3 partners LAMTOR2 in the Ragulator roadblock core
LAMTOR4 forms a roadblock heterodimer with LAMTOR5 that directly contacts the Rag roadblock domains
LAMTOR5 partners LAMTOR4 in the Ragulator roadblock core
MIOS is a beta-propeller subunit of the octameric GATOR2 assembly
NPRL2 contributes the longin domain that carries the catalytic residue for GAP activity toward RagA/B
NPRL2 is the catalytic subunit of the GATOR1 GAP: its Arg78 acts as the arginine finger, inserting into the RagA nucleotide pocket to stimulate GTP hydrolysis.
edges.notes: DEPDC5 provides the high-affinity Rag-binding surface of GATOR1 but is not catalytic; hydrolysis is driven through weaker NPRL2-NPRL3 contacts with RagA (Shen 2018).

edges.mechanism: NPRL3 bridges NPRL2 and DEPDC5 to complete the trimeric GATOR1 assembly
Rab1A is required for amino-acid-stimulated mTORC1 activation and interacts with Rheb on Golgi membranes; it is amplified and oncogenic in colorectal cancer
edges.notes: Independent replication of the Golgi Rheb-Rab1A interaction remains limited.

edges.mechanism: Rag-Ragulator provides the lysosomal docking site for FLCN-FNIP; during starvation FLCN is held inactive on RagA.GDP until amino acids are resupplied
Structural work defines the Ragulator-Rag assembly as the platform onto which mTORC1 docks at the lysosomal surface
The pentameric Ragulator clamps the Rag roadblock domains against the lysosomal membrane, providing the anchor without which the Rags cannot deliver mTORC1

Ragulator was reported to act as a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for RagA/B (Bar-Peled 2012), but later reconstitution found that it chiefly triggers GTP release from RagC, with SLC38A9 acting as the GEF for RagA.
edges.notes: Shen and Sabatini (2018) attribute the original RagA/B result to assay limitations, including possibly copurifying SLC38A9, while noting that Ragulator still alters the GTP affinity of RagA.

edges.mechanism: Under glucose starvation v-ATPase-Ragulator recruits AXIN-LKB1 to the lysosomal surface next to lysosomal AMPK; AXIN simultaneously blocks Ragulator GEF activity toward RagA/B, releasing mTORC1 from the lysosome.

The lysosomal E3 ligase RNF152 attaches K63-linked ubiquitin chains to RagA in an amino-acid-sensitive manner, creating a docking site that recruits GATOR1 and so promotes RagA GTP hydrolysis and mTORC1 inactivation.
edges.notes: Reported by a single laboratory (Deng 2015).

edges.mechanism: The lysosomal E3 ligase RNF152 mono-ubiquitinates Rheb at Lys8, increasing its affinity for the TSC complex and suppressing mTORC1; EGF stimulation acts through AKT-phosphorylated USP4, which deubiquitinates Rheb and releases it from the complex.
edges.notes: Reported by a single laboratory and not independently replicated in vivo; the same group identified RNF152 as the E3 ligase for RagA.

edges.mechanism: RUVBL1 (Pontin) binds the Tel2-Tti1-Tti2 module as part of the R2TP co-chaperone, whose PIH1D1 subunit recognises CK2-phosphorylated Tel2. The ATP-dependent TTT-RUVBL1/2 assembly is needed for mTOR stability, mTORC1 dimerisation and mTORC1 binding to the Rag GTPases.
edges.notes: RUVBL1 is not a subunit of TTT itself, which comprises Tel2, Tti1 and Tti2; energy depletion disassembles the TTT-RUVBL1/2 complex.

edges.mechanism: Energy-replete conditions drive TTT-RUVBL1/2 assembly, which promotes mTORC1 dimerisation and lysosomal localisation; energy stress dissociates the module and the dimer, coupling nutrient state to the oligomeric state of the complex.

RUVBL2 (Reptin) binds the Tel2-Tti1-Tti2 module together with RUVBL1 as part of the R2TP co-chaperone, whose PIH1D1 subunit recognises CK2-phosphorylated Tel2. The ATP-dependent TTT-RUVBL1/2 assembly is needed for mTOR stability, mTORC1 dimerisation and mTORC1 binding to the Rag GTPases.
edges.notes: RUVBL2 is not a subunit of TTT itself, which comprises Tel2, Tti1 and Tti2; energy depletion disassembles the TTT-RUVBL1/2 complex.

edges.mechanism: SEC13, also a COPII and nuclear-pore component, is a structural subunit of GATOR2
SEH1L, a WD40 protein shared with the nuclear pore complex, is a structural subunit of GATOR2
Under amino-acid starvation SH3BP4 binds the inactive Rag heterodimer and prevents formation of the active, mTORC1-recruiting configuration
edges.notes: Single primary report; not independently replicated or shown in vivo.

edges.mechanism: SCF-SKP2 attaches K63-linked ubiquitin chains to RagA and promotes GATOR1 recruitment, a negative feedback that limits amino-acid-dependent mTORC1 hyperactivation.
edges.notes: Single primary report; the acceptor lysines on RagA are not defined.

edges.mechanism: SZT2 binds GATOR1 directly and dictates GATOR control of mTORC1 signalling, acting as the pivotal contact within the scaffold
SZT2 not only nucleates KICSTOR but also contacts GATOR2, bringing GATOR1 and GATOR2 into one lysosomal supercomplex so that the sensor branch and the GAP branch are physically coupled.
edges.notes: SZT2 contacts both GATOR complexes; the GATOR2 arm is the less well defined of the two.

edges.mechanism: SZT2 is the very large fourth subunit around which the KICSTOR scaffold assembles
Loss of folliculin causes Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome with fibrofolliculomas, pulmonary cysts and renal tumours
Loss of FLCN causes Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome, in which mTORC1 signalling is dysregulated tissue-dependently rather than uniformly increased.
Germline FLCN loss abolishes RagC/D GAP activity, dysregulating mTORC1 in a tissue-dependent rather than uniformly increased manner
edges.notes: FLCN loss does not raise mTORC1 activity uniformly across tissues.

edges.mechanism: Without FLCN GAP activity RagC/D remains GTP-bound, so mTORC1 cannot phosphorylate TFEB at Ser211 even though it phosphorylates S6K1 and 4E-BP1 normally, and TFEB accumulates constitutively in the nucleus; removing TFEB rescues the renal phenotype of kidney-specific Flcn-knockout mice, indicating that this substrate-selective lesion rather than global mTORC1 hyperactivity drives it.
edges.notes: Consistent with the tissue-dependent rather than uniformly increased mTORC1 signalling seen in Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome.

edges.mechanism: FLCN loss removes the GAP for RagC/D; mTORC1 signalling is consequently dysregulated in a tissue-dependent rather than uniformly increased manner.
edges.notes: Direction of mTORC1 change is tissue-dependent, unlike the other proximal lesions.

edges.mechanism: Biallelic SZT2 mutations cause infantile encephalopathy with epilepsy and dysmorphic corpus callosum - the clinical proof that KICSTOR is non-redundant in humans
Biallelic SZT2 mutations cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome with epilepsy through loss of KICSTOR-dependent GATOR1 recruitment.
Biallelic SZT2 loss-of-function disables the scaffold, preventing GATOR1 recruitment and producing nutrient-insensitive mTORC1 activity
Biallelic SZT2 loss disables the KICSTOR scaffold required for GATOR1 lysosomal recruitment, the clinical proof that the scaffold is non-redundant in humans.
Within GATOR2, WDR24 is the subunit most strictly required for GATOR2 to inhibit GATOR1 and hence for amino-acid-dependent mTORC1 activation.
edges.notes: Subunit-level requirement from structural and genetic work; the molecular basis of GATOR2 inhibition of GATOR1 remains incompletely defined.

edges.mechanism: WDR24 is one of the five named subunits of the octameric GATOR2 assembly
WDR59 is a beta-propeller/RING-like subunit of the octameric GATOR2 assembly
AKT phosphorylates PRAS40 Thr246, promoting 14-3-3 binding and release of PRAS40 from Raptor; feed-forward derepression of mTORC1 by growth factors.
AKT phosphorylates PRAS40 at Thr246, releasing it from Raptor and derepressing mTORC1 - the feed-forward arm of growth-factor input, parallel to AKT inactivation of TSC2.
AKT phosphorylates BAD at Ser99, creating a 14-3-3 binding site that sequesters BAD and prevents it from neutralising BCL-XL; this survival output is favoured by Ser473-phosphorylated AKT.
AKT phosphorylates BAD to promote 14-3-3 binding and reduce its pro-apoptotic activity.
AKT phosphorylation of FOXO1 creates 14-3-3 sites and excludes it from the nucleus; output markedly enhanced by mTORC2-dependent Ser473 phosphorylation.
edges.notes: hepatic mTORC2→AKT→FOXO1 restrains gluconeogenesis (7.2).

edges.mechanism: Ser473 phosphorylation markedly enhances AKT activity toward FOXO1; phosphorylated FOXO1 binds 14-3-3 and is excluded from the nucleus.
edges.notes: Substrate-selective consequence of Ser473: mTORC2 biases AKT output toward survival and transcriptional programmes.

edges.mechanism: Ser473-dependent AKT activity phosphorylates FOXO1, excluding it from the nucleus and suppressing gluconeogenic gene expression; this is the step through which hepatic mTORC2 restrains gluconeogenesis.
AKT phosphorylates FOXO3a at three sites, promoting 14-3-3 binding and cytoplasmic retention, suppressing pro-apoptotic transcription.
FOXO3a phosphorylation by AKT is strongly Ser473-dependent, producing 14-3-3 binding and nuclear exclusion of a pro-apoptotic transcriptional programme.
AKT phosphorylates GSK3β Ser9 (GSK3α Ser21), creating a pseudosubstrate that inhibits the kinase; an mTORC1-independent AKT output retained with Thr308-only phosphorylation.
AKT phosphorylated only at Thr308 retains substantial activity toward GSK3β, so this output is largely independent of mTORC2.
edges.notes: Negative control for the Ser473-selective edges: it is why mTORC2 loss does not phenocopy AKT loss.

edges.mechanism: AKT retains mTORC1-independent output to GSK3beta; this is the stated reason distal-network lesions raise pathway flux without making the tumour dependent on the mTOR node.
AKT phosphorylates MDM2 Ser166/Ser186, promoting nuclear translocation and p53 ubiquitination; an mTORC1-independent AKT output.
edges.notes: MDM2 is one of the mTORC1-independent AKT outputs that make distal-network lesions poor predictors of rapalog sensitivity.

edges.mechanism: AKT phosphorylates MDM2, promoting nuclear entry and p53 turnover; part of the mTORC1-independent AKT output retained in distal-network lesions.
edges.notes: One of the mTORC1-independent AKT outputs that make distal-network lesions poor predictors of rapalog sensitivity.

edges.mechanism: AKT retains mTORC1-independent output to MDM2, and thus to p53, one of several branches showing that mTORC1 is only one effector downstream of AKT.

AKT phosphorylates TSC2 at five sites, Ser939 and Thr1462 being dominant, creating 14-3-3 binding sites; the demonstrated consequence is release of the TSC complex from the lysosomal membrane where Rheb resides, so Rheb·GTP accumulates. Stable dissociation of TSC1 from TSC2 remains poorly supported.
edges.notes: Part of the double-negative AKT -| TSC -| Rheb circuit. AKT phosphorylated only at Thr308 retains substantial activity toward TSC2 [387,388].

edges.mechanism: AKT phosphorylates and inactivates TSC2, permitting Rheb·GTP accumulation; this output is largely retained by Thr308-only AKT.
edges.notes: TSC2, like GSK3beta, is a Ser473-independent AKT substrate.

edges.mechanism: Insulin/AKT-dependent TSC2 phosphorylation releases the TSC complex from lysosomal membranes, physically separating the Rheb GAP from Rheb.
edges.notes: Conversely, amino-acid starvation recruits TSC2 to the lysosome via Rag GTPases (Demetriades 2014, PMID:24529380).

edges.mechanism: AKT phosphorylates the AMPK alpha1 ST-loop at human Ser487, reducing subsequent Thr172 phosphorylation by upstream kinases.
sites: Ser487 (human AMPK alpha1; Ser485 in rat)
edges.notes: Human alpha2 Ser491 is not assigned to AKT: Hawley et al. found alpha2 autophosphorylation at that site.

edges.mechanism: AKT phosphorylates mSin1 at Thr86, which one laboratory found to enhance mTORC2 activity toward AKT Ser473 and so create positive feedback. Another laboratory found that Thr86 and Thr398 phosphorylation, triggered by S6K or AKT depending on cell context, dissociates mSin1 from mTORC2 and suppresses its activity.
edges.notes: The sign of Thr86 phosphorylation is unresolved between the two laboratories. The 2015 study identified AKT, not S6K, as the main Thr86 kinase in every cell line tested.

edges.mechanism: Akt phosphorylates mTOR on Ser2448 downstream of PI3K; the site is a widely used activity biomarker but its functional consequence is disputed, and S6K1 phosphorylates the same residue, so the kinase assignment itself is contested.
AKT phosphorylates the Rab GAP AS160, creating a 14-3-3 site that relieves its restraint on GLUT4 storage vesicles.
Constitutively active AKT prevents denervation-induced atrophy in vivo.
Constitutively active AKT produces massive skeletal-muscle hypertrophy, establishing sufficiency of the AKT-mTOR arm for load-independent growth.
After mTOR-mediated priming, CK1alpha phosphorylates DEPTOR to complete the phosphodegron recognised by the SCF-betaTrCP ubiquitin ligase.
edges.notes: Gao and Duan (2011) place mTOR priming before CK1alpha phosphorylation of the degron, whereas Zhao (2011) attributes degron phosphorylation to S6K1 and RSK1.

edges.mechanism: DGKζ phosphorylates diacylglycerol to phosphatidic acid; the mechanically induced rise in PA and mTORC1 activity in muscle depends on DGKζ rather than on PLD.
edges.notes: From the Hornberger laboratory; qualifies the PLD-centred model [241,683].

edges.mechanism: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor at Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 (proline-directed), promoting Ras-dependent mTORC1 activation.
edges.notes: Direct phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser8, Ser696 and Ser863 by ERK1/2 rests mainly on one laboratory; Ser863 is also phosphorylated in an insulin- and mTOR-dependent manner. ERK and RSK input to mTORC1 is more commonly routed through the TSC complex rather than through Raptor.

edges.mechanism: ERK docks on the RSK C-terminus and phosphorylates the CTKD activation loop and linker; CTKD then autophosphorylates the hydrophobic motif (Ser380), creating the PDK1 docking site.
edges.notes: Site numbering is RSK1 (RPS6KA1).

edges.mechanism: ERK phosphorylates TSC2 (Ser664 principal), dissociating TSC1–TSC2 and functionally inactivating the complex; links Ras/MAPK activation to mTORC1.
ERK phosphorylates TIF-IA at Ser633, required for Pol I transcription and cell growth; an mTORC1-independent input to rRNA synthesis.

ERK1/2 phosphorylates UBF at Thr117 and Thr201 within HMG boxes 1 and 2, which prevents these boxes from binding DNA and alters UBF-induced rDNA architecture. This mediates the immediate activation of Pol I transcription by growth factors such as EGF.
ERK2 phosphorylates TFEB at Ser142 under nutrient-replete conditions, favouring cytoplasmic retention of TFEB and limiting expression of its lysosomal and autophagy target genes.
edges.notes: Ser142 is also phosphorylated by mTORC1, which is regarded as the main Ser142 kinase in amino-acid signalling; the contribution of ERK varies with cell type and stimulus.

edges.mechanism: MEK–ERK signalling couples photic stimulation to mTORC1 in the SCN: MEK inhibition blocks the light-induced rise in S6K1 and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation
edges.notes: Graded emerging for the SCN context specifically; the general ERK/RSK–TSC2 route belongs to growth_factor_input.

edges.mechanism: Farnesylation of the Rheb CAAX motif (Cys181) is required for endomembrane/lysosomal localisation and hence for mTORC1 activation.
The GRB2 SH3 domains bind the proline-rich C-terminus of SOS1 constitutively; receptor engagement relocates the GRB2–SOS1 complex to the plasma membrane next to Ras.
After AMPK priming at Ser1345, GSK3 phosphorylates TSC2 Ser1341/Ser1337, further activating TSC2; Wnt inhibits GSK3 and thereby relieves TSC2 to activate mTORC1, integrating Wnt and energy signals.
edges.notes: GSK3 phosphorylation requires prior AMPK phosphorylation of TSC2 at Ser1345. The numbering follows the original report; the same residues are Ser1379, Ser1383 and the priming site Ser1387 in the 1807-residue human sequence.

edges.mechanism: During ER stress, GSK-3beta phosphorylates Rictor at Ser1235, which interferes with binding of AKT to mTORC2 and lowers AKT Ser473 phosphorylation.
edges.notes: Single-laboratory report. Ser1235 is distinct from Thr1135, the Rictor site phosphorylated by S6K1.

edges.mechanism: HERC1 E3 ligase binds and ubiquitinates TSC2 not protected by TSC1, promoting its degradation.
edges.notes: Single primary study; physiological contribution relative to other TSC2 turnover routes not well quantified.

edges.mechanism: IKK-beta phosphorylates and suppresses TSC1, disinhibiting Rheb and therefore raising mTORC1 activity; this is one plausible molecular link between chronic inflammation and the anabolic dysregulation of ageing tissue.
edges.notes: Rests on a single laboratory's work (Lee DF et al., Cell 2007;130:440-455); the TSC1 Ser487/Ser511 assignment has not been independently replicated.

edges.mechanism: IKK-beta phosphorylates TSC1 Ser487/Ser511, suppressing TSC1 and the TSC complex so Rheb-GTP and mTORC1 activity rise; links inflammation to tumour angiogenesis and anabolic dysregulation.
edges.notes: The Ser487/Ser511 assignment derives from a single laboratory (Lee DF et al., Cell 2007;130:440-455) and has not been independently replicated at site level.

edges.mechanism: Stress-activated p38 MAPK phosphorylates and activates MK2.
MK2 phosphorylates TSC2 Ser1210, enhancing 14-3-3 binding; the net effect on Rheb-GAP activity and mTORC1 output is not firmly established.
edges.notes: Direction of effect on mTORC1 left as 'modulates' because functional readouts were limited.

edges.mechanism: MK2 phosphorylates ZFP36L1, inactivating its degradation of AU-rich-element-containing cytokine transcripts
MK2-dependent phosphorylation of the RNA-binding protein ZFP36L1 relieves degradation of SASP transcripts.
Dual-specificity MEK1/2 phosphorylate both residues of the ERK TEY activation-loop motif, Thr202 and Tyr204 in ERK1 and Thr185 and Tyr187 in ERK2, activating the kinases.
PDK1 phosphorylates the AKT activation loop at Thr308 once both are PIP3-bound; required for activity and, with Ser473, for full activation.
PDK1 phosphorylates the AKT activation loop; AKT requires this together with Ser473 for full activity.
After mTORC1 phosphorylates the S6K1 hydrophobic motif (Thr389), PDK1 phosphorylates the activation loop at Thr229 (p70 numbering), completing S6K1 activation.
edges.context: requires prior mTORC1 phosphorylation of S6K1 Thr389

edges.mechanism: After Thr389 priming, PDK1 phosphorylates the S6K1 activation loop at Thr229, completing kinase activation.
PDK1, recruited to the phospho-Ser386 hydrophobic motif, phosphorylates the NTKD activation loop, completing RSK activation.
edges.notes: Site numbering is RSK2 (RPS6KA3).

edges.mechanism: PHLPP1/2 directly dephosphorylate the AKT hydrophobic motif Ser473, terminating mTORC2-dependent activation and promoting apoptosis.
The B55α-containing PP2A holoenzyme dephosphorylates AKT Thr308, opposing PDK1 and restraining AKT output to TSC2/PRAS40.
After DNA double-strand breaks DNA-PKcs phosphorylates AKT Ser473 independently of mTORC2, promoting survival signalling.
edges.notes: A context-restricted alternative route to AKT Ser473 phosphorylation after DNA damage; mTORC2 remains the physiological hydrophobic-motif kinase for AKT.

edges.mechanism: RAF phosphorylates MEK1 Ser218/Ser222 (MEK2 Ser222/Ser226) in the activation segment.
edges.notes: MEK2 is phosphorylated at the equivalent residues Ser222 and Ser226. Phosphorylation of either serine is sufficient for maximal activation.

edges.mechanism: RSK phosphorylates Raptor at Ser719/721/722, increasing mTORC1 kinase activity downstream of oncogenic Ras/MAPK independently of TSC2.
RSK phosphorylates Raptor at an activating serine cluster downstream of oncogenic MAPK signalling, raising mTORC1 output independently of TSC.
edges.notes: Ser722 is also an AMPK target; the effect depends on the kinase and phosphorylation context.

edges.mechanism: RSK phosphorylates TSC2 C-terminal Ser1798 (and in vitro Ser939/Thr1462), inhibiting GAP function; the route by which phorbol esters and activated Ras raise mTORC1.
RSK1, activated downstream of ERK, was reported to phosphorylate the DEPTOR betaTrCP degron after growth-factor stimulation, promoting DEPTOR degradation and relieving mTOR inhibition.
edges.notes: RSK1 involvement rests on a single study; other work assigns degron phosphorylation to mTOR and CK1alpha.

edges.mechanism: p90RSK1 phosphorylates eEF2K at the same Ser366 site as S6K1, providing ERK-pathway control of elongation.
edges.notes: Supported by the same primary paper as the S6K1 claim [636].

edges.mechanism: RSK phosphorylates the same eIF4B Ser422 site as S6K1, so mTORC1 and Ras-ERK pathways converge on eIF4B.
Ras-ERK-activated RSK phosphorylates rpS6 at Ser235/236 independently of mTORC1, promoting cap-binding-complex assembly.
RSK phosphorylates TIF-IA at Ser649, cooperating with ERK Ser633 phosphorylation to activate Pol I transcription.
SOS1 catalyses GDP→GTP exchange on membrane-anchored Ras; Ras·GTP then engages RAF and the p110α Ras-binding domain.
One TBC1D7 subunit bridges the TSC1 coiled-coils in the 2:2:1 TSC1-TSC2-TBC1D7 assembly, which is the form that carries Rheb-GAP activity.

TBC1D7 binding to the TSC1 coiled-coil stabilises the TSC1-TSC2 association that presents the Rheb-GAP domain; its depletion weakens that association and reduces Rheb-GAP activity, raising mTORC1 signalling, without lowering TSC2 levels or altering TSC2 localisation to the lysosome.
TCTP was proposed as a Rheb guanine-nucleotide exchange factor in Drosophila; subsequent biochemical studies found no GEF activity.
edges.notes: Rheb's high intrinsic GTP loading makes a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor dispensable, and TSC2 GAP activity is treated as the sole regulator of its nucleotide state. Graded contested because the original Drosophila report is directly contradicted by later biochemistry.

edges.mechanism: TSC1 binding blocks HERC1-mediated ubiquitination of TSC2, stabilising tuberin; TSC2 protein is unstable without hamartin.
Two TSC1 (hamartin) copies form the coiled-coil scaffold of the 2:2:1 arch-shaped TSC1–TSC2–TBC1D7 complex.
TSC2 GAP domain accelerates Rheb GTP hydrolysis ~100-fold via an asparagine-thumb mechanism, converting Rheb·GTP to inactive Rheb·GDP; Rheb has no established GEF.
edges.notes: GAP polarity: TSC2 is the GAP (negative regulator); loss of TSC1/TSC2 gives constitutive Rheb·GTP and mTORC1 activation.

edges.mechanism: Two TSC2 (tuberin) copies supply the Rheb-GAP domains presented at the apex of the arch.

The TSC1–TSC2–TBC1D7 complex (2:2:1) presents the TSC2 GAP domain at its apex to lysosomal Rheb and accelerates GTP hydrolysis ~100-fold; in the absence of insulin the complex is held on the lysosome through Rheb and is released when AKT phosphorylates TSC2.
edges.notes: The complex is the GAP and inactivates Rheb; loss of TSC1 or TSC2 leaves Rheb GTP-loaded and mTORC1 constitutively active. Lysosomal retention of the complex and its insulin-dependent release were shown by Menon and colleagues.

edges.mechanism: The TSC1–TSC2 complex physically associates with mTORC2 and promotes its activity toward AKT, independently of its Rheb GAP function.
edges.notes: Polarity is opposite to the TSC-mTORC1 relationship.

edges.mechanism: Activated AMPK inhibits mTORC1 by two routes: phosphorylation of TSC2, which enhances its GAP activity toward Rheb, and direct phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser722 and Ser792, which creates 14-3-3 binding sites and imposes a metabolic checkpoint.
edges.notes: Net effect of the TSC2 and Raptor phosphorylation routes rather than a separate molecular event.

edges.mechanism: During acute energetic stress AMPK phosphorylates mTOR and Rictor within mTORC2, increasing mTORC2 activity toward AKT Ser473 and promoting cell survival, independently of its inhibition of mTORC1.
edges.notes: Single-laboratory study. In vitro, AMPK phosphorylated mTOR at Ser1261 and Rictor at unmapped sites, but Ser1261 was not required for AMPK-induced mTORC2 signalling, so the functionally relevant sites are unknown.

edges.mechanism: AMPK directly phosphorylates Raptor at two conserved serines, creating 14-3-3 binding sites that reduce mTORC1 kinase activity; imposes a metabolic checkpoint (G2/M arrest) independent of TSC2.
edges.notes: Both Raptor sites, including Ser792, are needed for the full checkpoint.

edges.mechanism: AMPK phosphorylates Raptor at Ser722/Ser792, directly inhibiting mTORC1 in parallel with its action on TSC2 and imposing a metabolic checkpoint.

Glucose deprivation-activated AMPK phosphorylates p53 Ser15, initiating a p53-dependent metabolic checkpoint (cell-cycle arrest) and transcription of sestrins, REDD1, PTEN and TSC2 that feed back on mTORC1.

Under energy stress AMPK phosphorylates TSC2 at Thr1271 and Ser1387, enhancing its GAP activity toward Rheb and lowering Rheb-GTP; this is required for energy-stress inhibition of mTORC1 and protects cells from apoptosis during energy deprivation.
edges.notes: Standard human TSC2 numbering (1807 residues); Inoki et al. 2003 [262] reported these residues as Thr1227 and Ser1345. AMPK phosphorylation at Ser1387 primes GSK3 phosphorylation at Ser1383 and Ser1379 (Ser1341 and Ser1337 in the Inoki numbering).

edges.mechanism: AMPK associates with ULK1 in a nutrient-dependent manner; the association is required for AMPK-mediated activating phosphorylation of ULK1 and is disrupted when mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757 (mouse numbering; Ser758 in human ULK1).
edges.notes: Phosphorylation at Ser757 acts by disrupting the ULK1-AMPK interaction.

edges.mechanism: Under glucose starvation AMPK binds and phosphorylates ULK1 at multiple sites, activating it to initiate autophagy/mitophagy; this is prevented when mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 Ser757.
edges.notes: Ser317/Ser777 from Kim 2011 [309]; Egan 2011 [157] additionally mapped Ser467, Ser555, Thr574 and Ser637.

edges.mechanism: Energy-stress-activated AMPK phosphorylates ULK1 at activating sites, initiating autophagy and mitophagy; blocked when mTORC1 has marked Ser757
edges.context: mouse ULK1 site numbering; energy-stress models
edges.notes: Mouse Ser555 corresponds to human Ser556; mouse Ser777 is not conserved in human ULK1. The effect of AMPK on autophagy depends on stress and timing.

edges.mechanism: AMPK phosphorylates CRY1, promoting FBXL3-dependent ubiquitination and degradation; this destabilises the clock's negative limb and entrains the oscillator to cellular energy state.
edges.context: mouse liver and fibroblasts; energy stress
edges.notes: Lamia 2009 reported Ser71 as the destabilising site, with a second site also described. PMID 19833968 (Science 2009;326(5951):437-440).

edges.mechanism: AMPK phosphorylates casein kinase 1ε at Ser389, increasing its activity toward PER2; a second route (besides CRY1) by which cellular energy status reaches the clock
edges.notes: External identifier requires independent verification.

edges.mechanism: Indirect relay: ROS-activated cytoplasmic ATM acts through LKB1 to increase AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation, and AMPK then phosphorylates TSC2, represses mTORC1 and induces autophagy; the response is lost in ATM-deficient cells, and no direct phosphorylation of AMPK by ATM has been shown.
edges.notes: Reported by one laboratory; the proposed ATM-LKB1 step is phosphorylation of LKB1 at Thr366.

edges.mechanism: ATM phosphorylates LKB1 at Thr366 (Thr363 in mouse) in response to ionising radiation and oxidative stress; the modification does not change LKB1 catalytic activity in vitro, but a non-phosphorylatable LKB1 mutant failed to restore ROS-induced mTORC1 repression in LKB1-deficient cells.
edges.notes: Two laboratories have reported ATM phosphorylation of Thr366, but its requirement for mTORC1 repression rests on a single study.

edges.mechanism: ATM phosphorylates p53 Ser15 (and CHK2, which phosphorylates Ser20), weakening MDM2 binding and stabilising/activating p53 after DNA damage.
Hypoxia-induced BNIP3 binds Rheb directly and lowers Rheb-GTP levels in a manner requiring its N-terminal domain, contributing to mTORC1 inhibition in hypoxia.
edges.notes: Reported by one group; mechanism of Rheb nucleotide change not fully defined.

edges.mechanism: REDD1-dependent mTORC1 inhibition requires TSC2 in the cited models. This functional relationship does not establish direct REDD1 binding to 14-3-3 or direct stimulation of TSC2 catalysis.
Direct REDD1 binding to 14-3-3 and displacement of TSC2 were proposed, but a subsequent structural and biochemical study did not detect REDD1-14-3-3 binding.
edges.notes: The direct binding mechanism is disputed; this does not negate REDD1-dependent suppression of mTORC1.

edges.mechanism: Phospho-eIF2alpha lowers ternary-complex availability; delayed reinitiation after uORF1 bypasses the inhibitory uORF2 so the ATF4 coding sequence is translated (integrated stress response).
edges.notes: Phosphorylation of eIF2alpha (an inhibitory event for eIF2) paradoxically increases ATF4 output.

edges.mechanism: PP2C-family phosphatases dephosphorylate AMPK Thr172 and switch the kinase off; AMP, and roughly ten-fold less potently ADP, binds the gamma-subunit CBS sites and protects Thr172 from dephosphorylation. This protection is distinct from the direct allosteric activation of the already phosphorylated kinase and is the main route by which a falling energy charge sustains AMPK activity.
edges.notes: Graded emerging because protection from dephosphorylation is established for the PP2C class while the physiological phosphatase isoform (PPM1A, PPM1B, PPM1E or PPM1F) remains unresolved.

edges.mechanism: Scaffolding beta subunit (beta1 or beta2) bridging alpha and gamma; its C-terminus binds both, its CBM binds glycogen and contributes to the ADaM drug site.

Regulatory gamma subunit (gamma1/2/3) whose four tandem CBS motifs form two Bateman domains with three occupied adenine-nucleotide sites: one holds AMP almost permanently, two exchange AMP, ADP and ATP, and one site remains unoccupied, conferring energy sensing on the heterotrimer.
p53 (and p63) bind the DDIT4/REDD1 promoter and induce it after DNA damage; REDD1 then releases TSC2 from 14-3-3 to suppress mTORC1.
p53 transcriptionally induces the AMPK β1 regulatory subunit, raising AMPK heterotrimer abundance as part of the same transcriptional programme that induces sestrins, TSC2 and PTEN.
edges.notes: The AMPK-subunit arm of the p53 transcriptional programme; induction is stress-, cell-type- and tissue-specific rather than general.

edges.mechanism: p53 binds a PTEN promoter element and induces PTEN; higher PTEN lowers PIP3-AKT, relieving AKT inhibition of TSC2 and reducing mTORC1 as one arm of the coordinated p53-mTOR response.
p53 binds response elements in SESN1 (PA26) and induces it after DNA damage; Sestrin1 contributes to p53-dependent mTORC1 suppression via GATOR2 binding and AMPK.
edges.notes: SESN1 (PA26) carries a functional p53-responsive element and is induced by genotoxic stress in a p53-dependent manner.

edges.mechanism: p53 induces SESN2 (Hi95) after genotoxic stress; Sestrin2 then inhibits mTORC1, principally by sequestering GATOR2, linking DNA damage to growth arrest.
edges.notes: Induction by DNA damage is p53-dependent, whereas induction by prolonged hypoxia or oxidative stress is largely p53-independent.

edges.mechanism: p53 transcriptionally induces TSC2 in a stress-, cell-type- and tissue-specific manner, raising Rheb-GAP capacity and reinforcing mTORC1 suppression after genotoxic stress.
edges.context: DNA damage; mouse tissues and cell lines
edges.notes: Induction is conditional rather than general; the dominant p53 route to mTORC1 runs through sestrins and AMPK. Induction of the AMPK beta1 subunit is documented in the same studies.

edges.mechanism: pVHL, the substrate-recognition subunit of a CUL2–elongin BC E3 ligase, binds prolyl-hydroxylated HIF-1α and polyubiquitinates it for proteasomal degradation; VHL loss in clear-cell renal carcinoma produces constitutive HIF signalling.
edges.notes: The normoxic degradation arm, relieved by hypoxia and by inhibition of the prolyl hydroxylases; VHL loss in clear-cell renal carcinoma produces constitutive HIF signalling.

edges.mechanism: Cdc37 binds the N-terminal nucleotide-binding domain of Hsp90, holds its lid open and inserts an arginine into the ATP pocket. This arrests the ATPase cycle while a client kinase is loaded.
Hsp90 acts with TTT/R2TP in maturing newly synthesised mTOR; Hsp90 inhibition destabilises mTOR and reduces mTORC1 signalling.
edges.notes: Second external ref removed: journal/volume did not match the claim (the geldanamycin/mTOR-raptor paper is Ohji et al. 2006, J Biochem 139:129-135, not BBRC 340:1125).

edges.mechanism: Tel2 binds Tti1 (and Tti2) to form the TTT module; loss of any subunit destabilises the others and lowers the steady-state level of all PIKKs including mTOR.

Tel2 binds the Tti1-Tti2 subcomplex through a conserved surface patch to form the TTT co-chaperone, which works with Hsp90 on newly synthesised PIKKs, including mTOR, to support their assembly into functional complexes.
Tti1 binds Tel2 and Tti2 to form the TTT module and, with Tel2, is required for mTOR stability and for assembly of mTORC1 and mTORC2.
loss of any one subunit destabilises the others.
Under nutrient sufficiency the TTT-RUVBL1/2 complex promotes mTORC1 dimerisation and its localisation to the Rag-Ragulator platform; energy stress disassembles it
edges.notes: The lysosomal-localisation arm rests largely on one laboratory, hence the emerging grade.

edges.mechanism: The TTT module binds nascent mTOR and, with R2TP/Hsp90, supports its folding; TTT depletion lowers mTOR protein and collapses signalling through both complexes.

Knockdown of Tti1 or Tel2 disassembles mTORC1 and mTORC2 as well as lowering mTOR levels, and Tel2 with Hsp90 is required to incorporate newly made mTOR into both complexes. This indicates a role in complex assembly beyond protein stabilisation.
The same TTT-dependent assembly requirement applies to mTORC2, whose integrity falls on Tti1-Tel2 depletion.
VPS34 is the catalytic lipid kinase of class III PI3K complex I, generating PI(3)P at the phagophore
PER2 acts within the PER–CRY repressor to inhibit CLOCK–BMAL1-driven transcription, setting the phase at which its own TSC1-dependent repression of mTORC1 occurs.
edges.notes: PER2 represses largely indirectly, through the PER–CRY complex and by controlling CRY nuclear entry, rather than by binding CLOCK–BMAL1 alone.

edges.mechanism: By recruiting TSC1 to the mTORC1 complex, PER2 suppresses mTORC1 activity in a time-of-day-dependent manner; the most direct clock-to-mTORC1 mechanism described.
edges.context: time-of-day dependent; maximal repression at peak PER2

edges.mechanism: PER2 heterodimerises with CRY proteins to form the PER–CRY repressor complex of the negative limb
PER2 engages the mTORC1 holocomplex (Raptor-containing) and scaffolds TSC1 onto it, which is how the TSC1 GAP arm is delivered to mTORC1 rather than acting only through the cytosolic TSC complex
edges.notes: PER2 scaffolds TSC1 to the mTORC1 complex; the complex-side partner RPTOR comes from the primary study, so the interaction is graded emerging pending further verification.

edges.mechanism: PER2 binds TSC1 and acts as a scaffold delivering it to the mTORC1 complex; the interaction is time-of-day dependent, tracking the circadian abundance of PER2.
AKT1 E17K in the PH domain increases PIP3-independent membrane association and constitutive Thr308/Ser473 phosphorylation.
edges.notes: AKT1 gain-of-function belongs to the distal-network lesions, without a specific primary citation.

edges.mechanism: Activating AKT1 alteration raises AKT output, which includes mTORC1-independent signalling to GSK3beta, FOXO and MDM2.
A mosaic somatic AKT1 c.49G>A (E17K) activating variant causes Proteus syndrome, present in affected tissues and absent from unaffected tissues of the same individuals.
PIK3CA, PTEN, AKT1 and receptor tyrosine kinase amplification make up the distal-network class.
Somatic mosaic activating AKT3 variants confined to malformed cortex drive mTORC1 hyperactivation causing hemimegalencephaly / focal cortical dysplasia type II.
Somatic mosaic AKT3 activation raises pathway output in the affected cortical lineage.
AKT3 is among the genes of focal cortical dysplasia type II, acting through somatic mosaic activation.
Somatic mosaic AKT3 activation causes hemimegalencephaly with hemispheric enlargement and severe epilepsy.

An NF2 nonsense mutation co-occurred with the TSC1 lesion in the index everolimus exceptional responder, and NF2 was one of five selection genes in the prospective basket study that did not demonstrate meaningful single-agent activity.
mTORC1 is activated on the cytosolic face of the lysosomal membrane, which is the point at which nutrient, growth-factor and stress information is spatially integrated
edges.notes: Lysosomal dysfunction in ageing and in lysosomal storage disease is a plausible upstream cause of mTOR dysregulation, not only a consequence.

edges.mechanism: Rheb resides on lysosomal/endomembrane surfaces, so mTORC1 can only meet GTP-loaded Rheb after Rag-dependent recruitment; cytosolic mTORC1 is effectively Rheb-free

During amino-acid starvation Rag-Ragulator traps FLCN-FNIP2 in the inactive lysosomal folliculin complex (LFC), holding FLCN's catalytic arginine finger away from the RagC nucleotide pocket; amino-acid refeeding releases the complex and licenses RagC/D GTP hydrolysis. This checkpoint explains why FLCN GAP activity is nutrient-gated.
edges.notes: Two independent cryo-EM structures (Lawrence 2019; Shen 2019) show FLCN-FNIP2 bound to RagA-GDP with the FLCN catalytic arginine away from the RagC nucleotide; Shen 2019 interprets this state as an on-pathway intermediate rather than an inhibitory trap.

edges.mechanism: The active Rag configuration tethers mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface; cryo-EM defines how mTORC1 docks onto the Rag-Ragulator assembly
Rag-mediated docking tethers mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface where Rheb-GTP is available; without it the complex remains diffusely cytosolic and cannot be activated.
RagA/B.GTP-RagC/D.GDP binds Raptor directly; this interaction is the physical basis of amino-acid-dependent mTORC1 localisation
RagA/B-GTP with RagC/D-GDP binds Raptor directly; the reciprocal nucleotide configuration releases it. The Rag-Raptor contact is a docking point, not an allosteric activator.
The Rag GTPases recruit TFEB (and MITF family members) to the lysosomal surface, which is the prerequisite for their phosphorylation by mTORC1
Amino-acid-loaded Rag GTPases recruit TFEB and MITF to the lysosomal surface, which is required for mTORC1 to phosphorylate them
RagA forms the obligate heterodimer with RagC or RagD through paired roadblock domains
Intersubunit crosstalk: the nucleotide state of one Rag biases the nucleotide state and GAP accessibility of its partner, enabling rapid switching with amino-acid availability
edges.notes: Crosstalk is reciprocal.

edges.mechanism: RagB is the functional paralogue of RagA and occupies the same position in the obligate heterodimer
RagC pairs with RagA/B through roadblock-domain contacts to form the obligate heterodimer
Phosphorylation of TFEB by mTORC1 requires RagC/D in its GDP state, making TFEB a substrate-specific output of the FLCN arm rather than of Rheb-driven mTORC1 activity
edges.notes: Substrate-selective output: TFEB phosphorylation depends on the nucleotide state of RagC/D rather than on bulk mTORC1 activity toward S6K1 and 4E-BP1.

edges.mechanism: RagD is the functional paralogue of RagC within the obligate heterodimer
FKBP38 was proposed to bind the mTOR FRB region and hold mTORC1 inactive until displaced by Rheb·GTP.
edges.notes: Independent laboratories found no effect of FKBP38 depletion or overexpression on mTORC1 signalling; retained only as a flagged contested model of how Rheb·GTP activates mTORC1.

edges.mechanism: GTP-loaded Rheb binds the N-HEAT, M-HEAT and FAT regions of mTOR, distal to the catalytic cleft, and allosterically realigns the FAT and kinase domains into a catalytically competent active site; lysosomal recruitment alone is insufficient for activation.
Rheb·GTP binds the mTOR N-HEAT/FAT region, realigning FAT and kinase domains (DFG motif, αC helix) into a catalytically competent state; needed after Rag-mediated lysosomal recruitment.
edges.notes: Recruitment by Rags is necessary but not sufficient; Rheb binding supplies activation [364].

edges.mechanism: Rheb-GTP binding realigns the N-HEAT, FAT and kinase domains, correcting the misaligned active site; this allosteric step is the proximate activation of lysosomal mTORC1.
Rheb·GTP was proposed to bind FKBP38 and release it from mTOR, de-repressing mTORC1.
edges.notes: Paired with FKBP8 → mTORC1; both contested.

edges.mechanism: Rheb·GTP binds and stimulates PLD1 in a GTP-dependent manner, providing a parallel phosphatidic-acid route to mTORC1 activation.
edges.notes: Limited independent replication; relative contribution versus direct Rheb–mTOR binding unclear.

edges.mechanism: Rheb·GTP binds the N-terminal region of B-Raf/C-Raf, reducing kinase activity and B-Raf–C-Raf heterodimerisation; an mTOR-independent crosstalk that dampens ERK output when TSC is lost.
edges.notes: Reported by more than one group but with variable magnitude; graded emerging.

edges.mechanism: GTP-loaded Rheb binds the N-terminal portions of the N-HEAT, M-HEAT and FAT domains about 60 Å from the kinase active site; the resulting movement twists the FAT clamp and realigns the DFG motif and alphaC helix into a catalytically competent active site.

Rheb-GTP binds across the mTOR N-HEAT, M-HEAT and FAT regions rather than at the catalytic cleft and activates the kinase allosterically [672]; earlier biochemical mapping localised the interaction to the kinase region [364].
Rheb-mTORC1 is required for Th1 and Th17 differentiation, with Rheb as the upstream element of this arm.
PRAS40 TOS motif occupies the Raptor substrate pocket and its N-terminal segment contacts mTOR, blocking S6K1/4E-BP1 access; substoichiometric mTORC1 component.
Structural work on the Rheb-bound complex shows PRAS40 occupying the substrate path, lowering mTORC1 output in the basal, growth-factor-deprived state.
PRAS40 is a substoichiometric mTORC1 subunit, associating through Raptor rather than contributing structurally to the dimer.
PRAS40 presents its own TOS motif to the Raptor substrate pocket and competes with S6K1 and 4E-BP1 for access, acting as a direct inhibitor of substrate binding.
Cullin-1 is the scaffold of the SCF(beta-TrCP) ligase.
DEPTOR engages the FAT region of mTOR through its PDZ domain, suppressing kinase output toward substrates of both complexes.
DEPTOR binding restrains mTORC1; its loss raises S6K1 and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation, and its overexpression in myeloma suppresses mTORC1 while relieving feedback onto PI3K-AKT.
DEPTOR associates substoichiometrically with mTORC1 as an inhibitory subunit.
DEPTOR is a substoichiometric inhibitory subunit of mTORC2 as well as of mTORC1.

DEPTOR binds mTORC2 and restrains its kinase activity, so DEPTOR loss increases phosphorylation of AKT Ser473 and SGK1. DEPTOR overexpression nevertheless activates AKT indirectly, by suppressing mTORC1 and relieving its feedback inhibition of PI3K.
beta-TrCP2 (FBXW11) is redundant with BTRC as the receptor for the DEPTOR phosphodegron.

mTOR phosphorylates DEPTOR at Ser293 and Ser299 (and Thr295), priming CK1alpha to phosphorylate the Ser286/Ser287/Ser291 degron, which SCF(beta-TrCP) binds, polyubiquitinates and sends for proteasomal degradation. Active mTOR thereby removes its own inhibitor in a positive-feedback loop.
edges.notes: Ser293 and Ser299 are mTOR priming sites outside the beta-TrCP degron. One study attributes degron phosphorylation instead to S6K1 and RSK1.

edges.mechanism: SKP1 adapts the F-box protein beta-TrCP to the CUL1 scaffold.

The ATP-binding cleft lies in the bilobed kinase domain of mTOR and is identical in mTORC1 and mTORC2, which is why agents that occupy it inhibit both complexes, unlike allosteric agents acting at the FRB domain.

The mSin1 CRIM domain is a ubiquitin-like fold whose acidic loop binds AGC-kinase substrates at a site distal to the catalytic cleft; the basic surface of the AKT kinase N-lobe engages this loop about 75 Å from the mTOR active site. CRIM-dependent recruitment also applies to SGK and PKC, although different AGC kinases differ in their sensitivity to perturbation of mSin1.
The CRIM domain is the central substrate-recruitment module of mSin1.

ETV7 is reported to interact with mTOR in the cytoplasm and to assemble a putative third complex, mTORC3, that lacks core mTORC1 and mTORC2 subunits and keeps mTOR activity in the presence of rapamycin. Tumour cells that lose this complex become rapamycin-sensitive.
edges.notes: Reported by a single laboratory and not widely replicated; mTORC3 remains an emerging concept.

edges.mechanism: The ETS repressor ETV7 is reported to nucleate the putative third complex and to confer rapamycin insensitivity on it.
edges.notes: Not independently replicated.

edges.mechanism: ETV7 is reported as the defining subunit of a putative third mTOR assembly, designated mTORC3, which is rapamycin-insensitive and supports proliferation in cancer cells.
edges.notes: A contested claim: single-laboratory description, not widely replicated, and the supporting evidence is weak.

edges.mechanism: The C-terminal FATC motif is integral to the kinase domain and packs against the activation loop and the mLST8-binding element. Deleting the conserved C-terminal residues, or substituting a conserved tryptophan within them, nearly abolishes mTOR kinase activity.
Extreme C-terminal FATC domain, the last structural element of mTOR, packing against the catalytic core.

The FAT clamp holds the kinase domain in a partially closed, low-activity conformation by distorting the active site; hyperactivating cancer mutations cluster at this FAT-kinase interface and Rheb binding relieves the restraint.
The FAT (FRAP-ATM-TRRAP) alpha-helical domain wraps around the kinase domain and is a defining feature of the PIKK family.

FRB sits at the entrance of the deep catalytic cleft and acts as a gatekeeper: its rapamycin-binding surface contacts substrates and gives them access to the recessed active site. FKBP12-rapamycin bound at FRB therefore restricts substrate access without occupying the ATP site.
The ~100-residue four-helix FRB bundle lies between the FAT and kinase domains of the mTOR polypeptide and forms the drug-binding surface.
The four-helix FRB domain lies between the FAT and kinase domains, above the substrate cleft, which is why an occupant of this site obstructs substrate entry.

The N-terminal HEAT repeats, arranged as N-HEAT (horn) and M-HEAT (bridge) segments, fold into an elongated alpha-solenoid. The solenoid contributes to the dimer interface and provides the docking surface for Raptor in mTORC1 and Rictor in mTORC2.
edges.notes: Domain-level decomposition of mTOR

edges.mechanism: PI3K-like catalytic domain carrying the ATP site in a deeply recessed cleft; it is the catalytic unit shared by mTORC1, mTORC2 and the putative mTORC3.

mTORC2 selects AKT by distal docking: the basic surface of the AKT kinase N-lobe engages an acidic loop of the mSin1 CRIM domain and the C-lobe a Rictor–mSin1 mooring ~75 Å from the active site; residues flanking Ser473 are dispensable, and prior engagement of pThr450 by the same N-lobe residues builds in a proofreading step.
edges.notes: The primary support is the 2025 enzyme-substrate structure [597]; the 'conserved tri-arginine cluster' formulation is inaccurate and should be avoided. The claim rests on this single structural study, with [74,483] as supporting cellular observations.

edges.mechanism: The basic surface of the Akt kinase N-lobe engages an acidic loop of the mSin1 CRIM domain ~75 A from the catalytic site; specificity is structural, not local sequence around Ser473.
edges.notes: Primary support is a single 2025 structural study; the widely repeated 'tri-arginine cluster' formulation should be treated with caution.

edges.mechanism: An acidic loop of the mSin1 CRIM domain engages the basic AKT N-lobe surface ~75 Å from the catalytic site, encoding substrate choice by distal docking rather than local sequence.
edges.notes: Residues flanking Ser473 are unimportant for phosphorylation. The same N-lobe residues engage phospho-Thr450, so AKT must change conformation first, which builds a proofreading step into substrate selection. The distal-docking geometry rests on a single structural study.

edges.mechanism: mSin1 is a defining mTORC2 subunit; its N-terminal segment binds Rictor and it is required for complex integrity and kinase activity toward Akt.
mSin1 binds Rictor through its N-terminal segment and maintains Rictor–mTOR complex integrity; its loss abolishes AKT Ser473 phosphorylation.
Sin1-dependent recruitment delivers PKC isoforms to mTORC2; mSin1 interface changes shift the balance of AGC substrates phosphorylated.
mSin1 CRIM-dependent recruitment of AGC kinases extends to protein kinase C isoforms; mTORC2 substrate preference among AGC kinases is modulated by subtle Rictor-mSin1 interface changes.
edges.notes: Graded emerging rather than established: [74] demonstrates Sin1-dependent recruitment of AGC kinases, but isoform-resolved dependence of each PKC on mSin1 is less completely shown than for AKT and SGK1.

edges.mechanism: The N-terminal region of mSin1 binds Rictor; the interface maintains complex integrity and its subtle variation modulates which AGC kinase is preferred.
The mSin1 CRIM domain recruits AGC-kinase substrates generally; different AGC kinases are differentially sensitive to perturbation of mSin1.

The central CRIM domain of mSin1 recruits AGC-kinase substrates generally, not AKT alone; Sin1-dependent recruitment is required for mTORC2 to phosphorylate SGK1, and different AGC kinases are differentially sensitive to perturbation of mSin1.
edges.notes: The SGK1 and PKC arms are missing.

edges.mechanism: mSin1 contributes with Rictor to occlusion of the FRB domain in assembled mTORC2.

In the basal state the mSin1 PH domain folds back onto the mTOR kinase domain and autoinhibits mTORC2. PIP3 binding to the PH domain relieves this autoinhibition and recruits the complex to the plasma membrane.
edges.notes: Reproduced across laboratories.

edges.mechanism: mLST8 docks onto the LBE (mLST8-binding element) of the kinase domain, adjacent to the active site, in both mTORC1 and mTORC2.
The mLST8 WD40 beta-propeller docks on the kinase domain near the activation loop and stabilises the catalytic conformation.
mLST8 contacts the kinase domain near the activation loop and stabilises the catalytic conformation.
mLST8 is present at two copies per mTORC1 dimer, its WD40 propeller abutting the kinase domain near the activation loop.
mLST8 deletion phenocopies Rictor rather than Raptor loss: mTORC2 signalling to Akt-FOXO and PKCalpha fails while S6K1 signalling is preserved.
mLST8 is a stoichiometric mTORC2 subunit contacting the kinase domain; unlike in mTORC1 its loss abolishes complex function.
WD40 β-propeller abutting the kinase domain near the activation loop
mTOR self-associates through the N-terminal HEAT repeat region, producing the obligate head-to-head dimer seen in both mTORC1 and mTORC2 cryo-EM reconstructions.
edges.notes: Self-loop representing homodimerisation of the catalytic subunit.

edges.mechanism: mTOR autophosphorylates Ser2481 in the C-terminal region adjacent to FATC; the mark reports intrinsic catalytic activity of assembled mTORC1 and mTORC2 rather than driving it.
Two mTOR protomers form the catalytic core of the ~1.1 MDa mTORC1 homodimer, facing one another across a dimer interface with the kinase domains at the obtuse vertices.
mTOR supplies the catalytic subunit of the ~1.0 MDa mTORC2 homodimer, resolved by cryo-EM at 3.2 A.
Two mTOR protomers form the catalytic core of the ~1.0 MDa mTORC2 homodimer, resolved by cryo-EM at 3.2 Å.
mTOR is reported to form an ETV7-containing assembly lacking Raptor and Rictor that retains activity in the presence of rapamycin.
edges.notes: Single-laboratory description; the existence and composition of mTORC3 remain contested.

edges.mechanism: mTOR is the catalytic subunit of the putative ETV7-containing mTORC3 assembly.
edges.notes: keeps mTORC3 connected to the catalytic tier.

edges.mechanism: mTOR phosphorylates Raptor at Ser863 within the complex, a rapamycin-sensitive intracomplex event that primes further multisite phosphorylation and supports mTORC1 activity.
mTOR associates with TFIIIC and is detected at tRNA and 5S rRNA genes, positioning it to target the repressor MAF1 at Pol III promoters.
edges.notes: Chromatin association shown by one laboratory; MAF1 phosphorylation itself is established.

edges.mechanism: Chromatin immunoprecipitation detects a nuclear pool of mTOR at rDNA and tRNA gene promoters, in a manner that depends on growth signals and is sensitive to rapamycin. This suggests chromatin-level control of Pol I and Pol III transcription, but a direct contact between mTOR and the polymerase has not been shown.
edges.notes: Single-laboratory ChIP finding.

edges.mechanism: mTOR signalling modulates central clock function in the suprachiasmatic nucleus and shapes the magnitude of photic entrainment, linking the kinase to phase control of behaviour.
edges.context: mouse SCN; central and peripheral clocks

edges.mechanism: Deletion of mTOR in the adult mouse myocardium causes a fatal dilated cardiomyopathy with cardiomyocyte apoptosis and accumulation of 4E-BP1, marking the lower bound of the cardiac therapeutic window for mTOR inhibition.

Mice with genetically reduced mTOR expression live longer and show a segmental, tissue-specific slowing of ageing, indicating that the lifespan effect of rapamycin reflects on-target mTOR inhibition rather than an off-target drug action.

mTOR signalling is required for oligodendrocyte differentiation and myelination. Loss of Raptor delays the onset of myelination, reduces sheath thickness and impairs differentiation in a region-dependent manner, most severely in spinal cord, whereas loss of Rictor has modest effects and combined loss is most severe, so mTORC1 is dominant and mTORC2 contributory.
Bone requires mTOR signalling for osteoblast differentiation.

The role of mTOR in osteoclast differentiation is unsettled: rapamycin suppresses RANKL-driven osteoclastogenesis in culture, whereas deletion of Raptor in osteoclast precursors has been reported to enhance differentiation and low-dose rapamycin can increase bone resorption in vivo. The net skeletal effect of inhibition is therefore context-dependent and not predictable from cell-autonomous data.
Deletion of mTOR in naive T cells favoured Foxp3-positive regulatory differentiation in the tested mouse model.
edges.context: de novo Treg differentiation; mouse T cells
edges.notes: This does not establish that mTOR universally inhibits mature Treg expansion or function.

edges.mechanism: Bone requires mTOR signalling for both osteoblast and osteoclast differentiation, so the net effect of inhibition is context-dependent and cannot be predicted from cell-autonomous data alone.
T cell-specific mTOR deletion abrogates Th1, Th2 and Th17 differentiation while promoting Foxp3+ regulatory T cell differentiation.
mTORC1 phosphorylates its own inhibitor PRAS40 (Ser183, Ser212, Ser221), weakening its binding to Raptor and reinforcing growth-factor-driven derepression.
mTORC1 phosphorylates and stabilises Grb10, increasing its abundance.
Direct mTORC1 phosphorylation stabilises Grb10 protein; identified by unbiased phosphoproteomics as a core mTORC1 substrate
edges.notes: Site numbering follows the phosphoproteomic reports; the stabilisation, not the exact residues, is the established claim.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of Grb10 stabilises the protein against degradation and raises its steady-state level; stabilised Grb10 binds and desensitises the insulin and IGF-1 receptors, forming one of the negative-feedback brakes on upstream signalling.
mTORC1 phosphorylates AMPK alpha2 Ser345 (Raptor-dependent) under nutrient stress, suppressing AMPK activity and promoting proliferation: a reciprocal brake opposing AMPK inhibition of mTORC1.
edges.notes: Single-laboratory finding awaiting independent replication; a reciprocal brake opposing AMPK inhibition of mTORC1.

edges.mechanism: In nutrient sufficiency mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757 (mouse numbering; human Ser758), disrupting the ULK1-AMPK interaction and preventing AMPK-mediated activating phosphorylation at Ser317, Ser555 and Ser777; AMPK and mTORC1 therefore toggle autophagy initiation.

ULK1 Ser637 (mouse numbering; human Ser638) is dephosphorylated during nutrient starvation and its phosphorylation falls with mTOR inhibition, but the same site is also assigned to AMPK, so the responsible kinase is unresolved.
edges.context: mouse site numbering; human experiments in Shang 2011
edges.notes: The kinase assignment for this site conflicts between studies, and the consequences for ULK1-AMPK binding differ between experimental systems.

edges.mechanism: Active mTOR phosphorylates DEPTOR in the linker between its DEP and PDZ domains. This primes the degron for CK1alpha and marks DEPTOR for betaTrCP-dependent degradation, so active mTOR removes its own brake.
edges.notes: Zhao et al. 2011 attributed degron phosphorylation to S6K1 and RSK1 rather than to mTOR directly.

edges.mechanism: Through 4E-BP phosphorylation and the S6K1-eIF4B/PDCD4/eEF2K axis, mTORC1 stimulates cap-dependent initiation and elongation. The effect is selective rather than global, and the most mTORC1-sensitive mRNAs, mainly TOP and TOP-like transcripts, depend chiefly on the 4E-BPs.
Rapamycin-sensitive phosphorylation of eEF2K at Ser78 (adjacent to the calmodulin-binding site) impairs calmodulin binding and eEF2K activity; direct kinase not definitively identified.
edges.notes: Site is mTOR-dependent; whether mTORC1 phosphorylates it directly is unresolved.

edges.mechanism: Growth factors and nutrients recruit mTOR-Raptor to the eIF3 preinitiation complex, where mTORC1 phosphorylates S6K1 and 4E-BP1 through dynamic protein interchange.
mTORC1 first phosphorylates priming sites Thr37/Thr46; these are largely rapamycin-resistant, which is the structural reason rapalogs incompletely suppress cap-dependent translation.
edges.notes: Priming step of the hierarchical mechanism.

edges.mechanism: After Thr37/46 priming, mTORC1 phosphorylates Thr70 then Ser65 in a TOS-dependent, rapamycin-sensitive manner, lowering eIF4E affinity by orders of magnitude and releasing eIF4E.
edges.notes: Ser65 phosphorylation additionally requires Ser101 (Wang 2003).

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP2 at Thr37, Thr46, Ser65 and Thr70, the residues equivalent to the 4E-BP1 sites, in a rapamycin-sensitive manner that releases eIF4E. Loss of both 4E-BP1 and 4E-BP2 makes TOP and TOP-like mRNA translation resistant to mTOR inhibition.
Serum-stimulated, rapamycin-sensitive phosphorylation of the eIF4GI C-terminal region; direct kinase and functional consequence not firmly established.
edges.notes: mTOR-dependent but may be indirect.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates a C-terminal cluster of LARP1 sites adjacent to the DM15 region, weakening cap/TOP binding and releasing TOP mRNAs for eIF4F-dependent translation.
edges.notes: mTORC1 phosphorylates at least 26 rapamycin-sensitive serine and threonine residues on LARP1, arranged in seven clusters. The cluster next to the DM15 region is the most rapamycin-sensitive.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 directly phosphorylates the Pol III repressor MAF1 at Ser60/68/75 in a rapamycin-sensitive manner, inactivating it and derepressing tRNA and 5S rRNA transcription.
mTORC1 coordinates Pol I (TIF-IA/UBF), Pol III (MAF1) and Pol II/TOP-mRNA (LARP1) outputs so that rRNA, tRNA and ribosomal-protein pools scale together.
mTOR phosphorylates the S6K1 turn motif at Ser371 in vitro. Ser371 phosphorylation is required for Thr389 phosphorylation and for intrinsic kinase activity.
edges.notes: In cells, GSK3 also phosphorylates Ser371, and mTOR maintains phosphorylation of this site partly by restraining its dephosphorylation.

edges.mechanism: Raptor-TOS-recruited S6K1 is phosphorylated by mTORC1 on hydrophobic-motif Thr389, creating the docking site that permits PDK1 activation-loop phosphorylation.
edges.notes: Thr389 phosphorylation is fully rapamycin-sensitive.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 drives rapamycin-sensitive phosphorylation of Thr388 in the S6K2 hydrophobic motif, the equivalent of S6K1 Thr389. A phosphomimetic Thr388Glu substitution makes S6K2 fully active and resistant to rapamycin.
Adipocyte Raptor deletion impairs adipogenesis and reduces fat mass with enhanced mitochondrial respiration, placing mTORC1 upstream of the storage programme
Adipocyte Raptor deletion impairs adipogenesis and reduces fat mass with enhanced mitochondrial respiration; the PPARgamma programme is the mTORC1 output of adipose tissue.
Through S6K1-IRS-1 and Grb10, active mTORC1 restrains PI3K-AKT; relief of both brakes on mTORC1 inhibition produces rebound AKT activation
mTORC1 phosphorylates AMBRA1, preventing AMBRA1-TRAF6-mediated ULK1 ubiquitylation, self-association and activation
edges.notes: Ser52 of human AMBRA1 is the mapped mTOR site; its dephosphorylation on mTOR inhibition allows AMBRA1 and TRAF6 to drive Lys63-linked ubiquitylation of ULK1.

edges.mechanism: In proliferating cells with high mTORC1 activity, ATF4 (CREB2) protein has been reported to undergo proteasome-dependent degradation, lowering SIRT4 transcription and thereby relieving SIRT4-mediated inhibition of glutamate dehydrogenase.
edges.context: glutamine metabolism and SIRT4 repression in proliferating cells
edges.notes: This is opposite in sign to the mTORC1-dependent translational induction of ATF4 reproduced in several laboratories for purine, one-carbon and glutathione synthesis; the degradation arm rests on a single study and the conditions that reconcile the two are unknown.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 raises ATF4 protein by translational control independent of eIF2alpha phosphorylation, balancing amino-acid supply against demand
mTORC1 phosphorylates ATG13 within the ULK1 initiation complex, contributing to layered repression of phagophore initiation
edges.notes: Ser258 has been identified as a direct mTOR site on ATG13; how much ATG13 phosphorylation contributes to autophagy repression relative to ULK1 phosphorylation remains debated.

edges.mechanism: mTOR phosphorylates ATG14 at five mapped sites, suppressing the ATG14-containing VPS34 complex; mutation of all five sites reduces this inhibition.
edges.notes: The five residues were mapped by in vitro kinase assays and mutagenesis; ATG14 lacking all five sites escapes mTORC1-mediated inhibition of the associated VPS34 activity.

edges.mechanism: Amino acids released by completed autolysosomal degradation reactivate mTOR, and this reactivation is required for autophagic lysosome reformation, the tubulation and scission of autolysosomal membranes that regenerates functional lysosomes and terminates the autophagic cycle.
edges.context: late phase of a completed autophagic cycle

edges.mechanism: Through phosphorylation of ULK1 at Ser758 (Ser757 in mouse) and of ATG13, ATG14L and AMBRA1, mTORC1 imposes layered repression of phagophore initiation.
mTOR is required for expression of the sterol biosynthetic gene programme through SREBP2
mTORC1 directly phosphorylates the acetyltransferase p300, increasing its activity toward autophagy and lipogenic substrates

mTORC1 represses SIRT4 transcription by promoting proteasomal degradation of CREB2 (ATF4), relieving SIRT4-mediated inhibition of glutamate dehydrogenase and increasing entry of glutamine-derived alpha-ketoglutarate into the TCA cycle.
edges.notes: A proposed second arm, S6K1–eIF4B-dependent translation of c-Myc driving glutaminase expression, rested on a study that has since been retracted.

edges.mechanism: Glycolytic flux rises through cap-dependent translation of HIF-1alpha and consequent induction of GLUT1, HK2, PFKFB3, PKM2 and LDHA
mTOR signalling contributes to metabolic adaptation during T-cell activation; the contribution of this complex depends on lineage and stimulation conditions.
edges.notes: The cited differentiation study does not establish a universal requirement for both complexes in all T-cell metabolic programmes.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 raises HIF-1alpha synthesis through 4E-BP1/eIF4E- and S6K1-dependent cap-dependent translation of HIF1A mRNA, including under normoxia in TSC-deficient cells. Separately, a TOR signalling (TOS) motif in HIF-1alpha binds Raptor and is required for full HIF-1alpha transcriptional activity, a protein-level mechanism distinct from translational control.
mTOR-dependent translation raises IL-1alpha, which drives NF-kB-dependent amplification of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype
mTOR promotes IL1A translation, which drives the pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype; one of the two defined mechanisms behind the mTORC1 requirement for SASP.

mTORC1 has been reported to phosphorylate IRS-1 directly at Ser636/Ser639, with Raptor acting as a scaffold, in a rapamycin-sensitive manner; phosphorylation of these serines next to the Tyr632 PI3K-binding motif impairs IRS-1-associated PI3K activation and contributes to nutrient-induced insulin resistance.
edges.notes: Other studies attribute Ser636/Ser639 phosphorylation to S6K1, so the relative contributions of mTORC1 and S6K1 at these residues are unresolved.

edges.mechanism: De novo lipogenesis proceeds through SREBP1, with mTORC1 acting both by phosphorylating Lipin1 and by promoting SREBP processing
edges.context: growth-factor and nutrient sufficiency; in liver, contributes to steatosis under hyperinsulinaemic conditions
edges.notes: Hepatic mTORC1 is required for insulin-induced SREBP1c and lipogenesis but is not sufficient on its own, because parallel AKT signalling is also needed.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates Lipin1 and retains it in the cytoplasm, preventing its nuclear entry; Lipin1 is a direct mTORC1 substrate
edges.notes: Site numbering follows the mouse Lipin1 phosphosites reported in the primary study.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 reactivation during prolonged starvation terminates autophagy and drives autophagic lysosome reformation, regenerating the lysosomal pool
By holding TFEB and TFE3 out of the nucleus, mTORC1 suppresses CLEAR-driven expansion of the lysosomal compartment
Mitochondrial biogenesis is supported through 4E-BP-dependent translation of mitochondrial mRNAs and the YY1-PGC-1alpha axis
mTORC1 raises c-Myc protein by phosphorylating 4E-BP1 and releasing eIF4E for cap-dependent translation of MYC mRNA, whose structured 5′ untranslated region makes it highly eIF4F-dependent.
The oxidative pentose phosphate pathway is activated through SREBP-driven G6PD expression downstream of mTORC1

Amino-acid-dependent, rapamycin-sensitive mTOR kinase activity is required for the transactivation activity of PPARgamma during adipocyte differentiation; rapamycin disrupts the C/EBPalpha–PPARgamma positive feedback loop, and the PPARgamma ligand troglitazone reverses this block.
mTORC1 activity increases PPARG mRNA and protein expression during adipocyte differentiation; rapamycin lowers PPARgamma and C/EBPalpha expression and impairs adipogenesis.
Purine synthesis is driven through ATF4-dependent induction of MTHFD2 and control of the mitochondrial tetrahydrofolate cycle
Pyrimidine synthesis is stimulated acutely by the mTORC1-S6K1-CAD Ser1859 axis, coupling growth signalling to nucleotide supply
mTORC1 phosphorylates Pacer, blocking its engagement of HOPS and STX17 and thereby autophagosome-lysosome fusion; also couples to lipid metabolism
edges.notes: Single-group finding External reference not independently verified.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1-driven translation is required for the senescence-associated secretory phenotype; rapamycin suppresses the SASP without eliminating senescent cells
edges.notes: Intervention efficacy alone does not establish causal primacy of mTOR in ageing.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1-driven translation is required for the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, through IL1A and MAPKAPK2 translation.
mTORC1 represses SIRT4 expression by promoting proteasomal degradation of CREB2, de-repressing glutamate dehydrogenase
edges.notes: Rests on a single principal study, which attributes SIRT4 repression to mTORC1-dependent destabilisation of CREB2 (ATF4) rather than to a defined S6K1 step; this repression underlies the glutamate dehydrogenase limb of glutamine anaplerosis.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 promotes SREBP1 processing and nuclear accumulation, both by phosphorylating Lipin1 and by supporting proteolytic maturation
Hepatic mTORC1 promotes SREBP1c processing and activity, driving the lipogenic programme of the liver.
edges.notes: mTORC1 is necessary but not sufficient for insulin induction of hepatic SREBP1c: Akt must also suppress INSIG2a, and liver-specific Tsc1 loss alone protects against diet-induced steatosis.

edges.mechanism: mTOR activity is required for SREBP2-dependent sterol biosynthetic gene expression; part of this transcriptional profile is rapamycin-resistant
Rapamycin-sensitive, mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of the STAT3 transactivation domain at Ser727 enhances STAT3 transcriptional output
edges.notes: Whether mTOR acts directly or through an intermediate kinase is not fully settled.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates TFE3 at the site equivalent to TFEB Ser211, creating a 14-3-3 site and enforcing cytoplasmic retention
edges.notes: External reference not independently verified.

edges.mechanism: Phosphorylation at Ser142 acts with Ser211 to restrain TFEB nuclear translocation and CLEAR-network output
edges.notes: Ser142 is also an ERK2 site (assigned in ref [543]), so this residue integrates more than one input; the mTORC1-dependent assignment rests on ref [544].

edges.mechanism: Phosphorylation at Ser211 creates a 14-3-3 binding site that retains TFEB in the cytoplasm and prevents nuclear import
edges.notes: Ser122 has also been reported as an mTORC1 site contributing to cytoplasmic retention.

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 also phosphorylates TFEB at Ser122; a phosphomimetic Ser122 substitution keeps TFEB cytoplasmic after mTORC1 inhibition even when Ser211 is dephosphorylated, and blocks Torin1-induced lysosomal biogenesis.
edges.notes: The Ser122 site has been reported by a single laboratory (Vega-Rubin-de-Celis 2017).

edges.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates UVRAG at Ser498, enhancing RUBCN binding and suppressing UVRAG-dependent autophagosome and endosome maturation
mTORC1 phosphorylation of WIPI2 promotes its HUWE1-dependent ubiquitination and degradation, limiting recruitment of the ATG16L1 conjugation machinery
edges.notes: Single principal report External reference not independently verified.

edges.mechanism: mTOR associates with YY1 and is required for the YY1-PGC-1alpha interaction at mitochondrial gene promoters; rapamycin disrupts the complex

mTOR hyperactivation raises BMAL1 protein abundance by increasing its translation and altering its degradation and nuclear localisation, producing abnormal timekeeping in constant conditions and exaggerated responses to phase resetting; halving Bmal1 gene dosage rescues the circadian behaviour.
mTOR inhibition attenuates light-induced PER1 (and PER2) expression in the SCN and blunts photic phase shifts, indicating mTORC1-dependent amplification of the entrainment signal.
edges.notes: The finding (rapamycin blunts light-induced PER expression and phase shifting) comes from the Obrietan laboratory's SCN work. External reference not independently verified.

edges.mechanism: mTOR hyperactivation in a paradigmatic mTORopathy model produces circadian behavioural abnormalities downstream of aberrant BMAL1 proteostasis.
mTOR activity sets free-running period: genetic or pharmacological reduction of mTOR signalling lengthens the period of molecular and behavioural rhythms in SCN explants, peripheral cells and mice
edges.notes: Effect sign encodes 'shortens period'; the inhibitory sign is relative to period length, not to clock function.

edges.mechanism: mTOR signalling in the suprachiasmatic nucleus modulates central clock function and the magnitude of light-induced phase shifts and re-entrainment
The PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis is the most frequently altered growth-promoting pathway in human cancer, with activating lesions in roughly 30-50% of tumours depending on type and sequencing depth.
Elevated mTORC1 activity contributes to cyst growth in polycystic kidney disease; trials were limited by dose-related toxicity rather than by absence of rationale.
Chronic mTORC1 hyperactivation drives beta-cell dedifferentiation and failure through ER stress and suppressed autophagy.

mTORC1 supports the glutaminolytic reprogramming that accompanies effector T-cell activation, alongside the glycolytic switch, acting through Myc-dependent glutaminase expression and increased glutamine anaplerosis.
Chronic mTORC1 hyperactivation initially expands beta-cell mass and insulin secretion, before dedifferentiation and failure supervene.
edges.context: pancreatic beta-cell; early phase of hyperactivation

edges.mechanism: Hepatic mTORC1 suppresses fasting-induced ketogenesis by promoting nuclear retention of NCoR1 and thereby inhibiting PPARalpha.
edges.notes: Hepatic mTORC1 tone rises with age while ketogenic capacity falls, so listing ketogenesis among mTORC1-dependent hepatic outputs without a sign is ambiguous: the primary data show suppression rather than support.

edges.mechanism: mTOR-dependent dendritic translation underlies the late protein-synthesis-dependent phase of LTP; rapamycin blocks L-LTP while sparing the early phase.

mTOR promotes 4E-BP1-dependent translation of MAPKAPK2 (MK2) in senescent cells; MK2 phosphorylates the RNA-binding protein ZFP36L1 and blocks its degradation of SASP transcripts, sustaining the secretory phenotype.
